#2652. 2026-27 NBA Minutes Report: Brandon Ingram returns, Cameron Boozer is sidelined, more

Welcome to the NBA Minutes Report. Every week, I will review each team's updated minutes per game to see which players are seeing the court more or less than in previous weeks and what their impact has been. That can help you with any fantasy basketball decisions you may need to make, but also help you get a lay of the land on what's happening around the NBA and which players are gaining or losing value.

The charts below are also great for exploring on your own. You can track the minutes over the last three, five, ten games, and for the entire season, to see which trends stand out to you. All of this data was made accessible by Kyle Bland, who is incredibly talented and also extremely generous. Be sure to follow him to check out all of his baseball data as well.

We've now seen a full week with CJ McCollum (calf) on the bench, and that's given us slightly more minutes for Corey Kispert(who had 18 points on Sunday) and Lu Dort. However, most of the minutes are just going to the starters. Jock Landale has also been nursing a hip injury, which has created an opportunity for Zuby Ejiofor to enter the rotation.

Mitchell Robinson has been dealing with an illness, but his time in Boston has not gone well. In fact, things are not going well in Boston overall. They beat the Wizards on Tuesday, but had lost four straight games before that, including losses to the Kings and Warriors. Derrick White's shooting has been an issue again this season, and the Celtics just aren't consistently getting strong production from their best unit either.

Sadly, Nolan Traore suffered a hamstring injury that's going to sideline him for a few months. The Nets are likely going to spread playing time around for their young players, but Mikel Brown Jr. got 29 minutes on Monday and scored 17 points with five rebounds and seven assists. He also had six turnovers, but he's gonna have the ball in his hands far more often. The rest of the fill-in players aren't overly interesting.

Kon Knueppel, Grayson Allen, and Dennis Schroder all remain sidelined, so Sion James continues to start and play big minutes. There's not a ton of production, but he's a role player. Christian Anderson scored 25 points in 25 minutes on Monday, and this was a bit of a "hot hand" situation, but there aren't that many options off the bench right now. The rest of the bench totaled just six points in that game.

As we mentioned last week, we've slowly started to see Nic Claxton's minutes tick up. He played 23 in a win over the Cavaliers on Monday but had sat out the game against the Nuggets before. Norman Powell is now dealing with a hamstring injury, so Buddy Hield has stepped into the starting lineup and had 17 points and five rebounds in 27 minutes in that game on Monday. He is going to shoot when he's on the court.

Evan Mobley remains sidelined with a toe injury, which has shortened the Cavs' rotation. Sam Merrill is starting, and Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor have become the two key contributors off the bench. The rest is pretty much status quo here, and the usage sits heavily with the starters.

Caleb Martin's role continues to grow as a starter in Dallas. He played 30 minutes in their win over the Nuggets on Tuesday, scoring 13 points with four rebounds, four assists, and five steals. He's been a great complement to scorers like Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving. Morez Johnson Jr. has also clearly earned the backup big man role, ahead of Santi Aldama.

The Nuggets had been playing well before their loss to the Mavericks, and a lot of that has to do with how elite Nikola Jokić and Jamal Murray are as a duo, which I covered in a video this week. The Nuggets also have a clear-cut starting five, and then like to use Spencer Jones as their sixth man, but the rest of the bench is a rotating group that all seems ot play around 10-17 minutes depending on the matchup.

Cade Cunningham missed Tuesday's win over the Magic with a knee injury, which led to 35 minutes for Daniss Jenkins. We also saw Isaiah Joe start and play 30 minutes in that win, scoring 21 points with four rebounds. He seems to be settling into a larger role now that he's back from injury and Duncan Robinson is still out. The Pistons need his ability to space the floor.

The Warriors have deepened their rotation in the wake of all their injuries, but also 6-7 players are really playing meaningful minutes. Gui Santos did play 23 minutes in a win over the Celtics on Sunday, but that was because he was having a solid game overall. We finally saw De'Anthony Melton play 27 minutes in that game, but he was 0-7 from the field. Charles Bassey has become the starting center and had 13 points, 9 rebounds, 3 assists, and 3 steals in that win over the Celtics. He's been pretty good for Golden State.

The Rockets run one of the tightest rotations in basketball, and not much has changed with it over the last week. In fact, they don't have a single player listed on the injury report.

T.J. McConnell is dealing with a hamstring injury, which has led to more time for Braden Smith, who started and played 24 minutes in Monday's game against the Thunder. Jalen Slawson also played 20 minutes in that game and scored 16 points with 10 rebounds and four blocks, which is insane production in that many minutes. He could earn a larger role for himself.

We saw Brandon Ingram make his season debut on Monday night, which I recorded a video about. That led to a decrease in minutes for Max Strus and Gradey Dick, and Dick could be out of the rotation entirely. Yanic Konan Niederhäuser also returned to the court, which has pushed Isaiah Jackson down the pecking order.

Austin Reaves remains out with a heel injury, so Quentin Grimes and Matisse Thybulle remain in key roles in this rotation. Jake LaRavia has been in the starting lineup and off the bench, but he still pushes 30 minutes a night, and the rest of the team has had sporadic production off the bench. It's a solid bench, but there isn't really one guy they lean on constantly, apart from knowing that Collin Sexton is going to get up shots when he's in the game.

Sadly, the big news in Memphis was that Cameron Boozer will be sidelined for at least a month with a sprained ankle. With Jerami Grant and GG Jackson also hurt, there are some questions about the depth on the wing in Memphis, all of which I discussed in a video this week.

The Heat are starting to figure some things out. They beat the Thunder on Sunday for their seventh win in a row, and that was without Giannis Antetokounmpo, who missed with a groin injury. Bobby Portis Jr. started for him, but he'll move back to the bench on Wednesday with Giannis back. We have seen Ryan Conwell take on a much bigger role off the bench, playing at least 26 minutes in each of the last five games.

The Bucks are really not good and have just two wins this season. Of course, one of them happened in their last game against the Raptors. They essentially used just an eight-man rotation in that game, with Nate Ament, Kel'el Ware, and Brayden Burries as the only bench players playing over eight minutes. Burries has been a tremendous success for the Bucks so far this season, and there's some freedom for him in coming off the bench and just playing with his hair on fire.

The Timberwolves continue to play well with Anthony Edwards sidelined, and a big reason for that is Jaden McDaniels. We've now seen an extended period of time after Dejounte Murray demanded a trade, and Jeremiah Fears has unsurprisingly seen his role grow. Trey Murphy III will also play plenty of minutes, but he's not as much of a high-usage player as the other two. Saddiq Bey and Jordan Poole are the key pieces off the bench and fill flash, as they did on Monday against the Suns, but the production is not consistent.

The early-season struggles for Mikail Bridges and Josh Hart seem to be a little bit more in the rearview, and both players are trending back to their old roles with the Knicks finding their footing. OG Anunoby missed Sunday's game with a calf injury, which allowed Landry Shamet to start and Jose Alvarado to play 22 minutes off the bench, but it's not expected to be a long-term injury.

The Thunder lost Alex Caruso to a hip injury in addition to the larger injuries to Chet Holmgren, Cason Wallace, and Jalen Williams. As a result, Bennett Stirtz has seen his role grow. The production has been inconsistent, but the minutes might be there in the short term. Aday Mara missed Monday's game with a shin bruise, but he has been tremendous as a starter and figures to be a key part of this lineup for much of the season.

The Magic are now 7-10 and continue to struggle without Paolo Banchero. Franz Wagner is playing well, but Jalen Suggs is shooting just 32% from the field in November. Anthony Black is providing decent minutes in the starting rotation, but there isn't enough firepower off the bench to help carry this team when the starting lineup isn't delivering.

Not much has changed for the 76ers, but Dominick Barlow did make his season debut, and he'll likely be one of the key reserves, but will play fewer minutes with Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Anfernee Simons, and Dean Wade all in town now. Joel Embiid has continued to play big minutes when he does play, but he's missed four games for various reasons, which will happen throughout the season. The bench guys are gonna have spike weeks when some of the starters sit, but there won't be enough usage to go around when the team is healthy.

Status quo here from the Suns. Ryan Dunn has seen his role decrease a bit, and the Suns' bench unit led by Collin Gillespie and Jordan Goodwin is more interesting than their ill-fitting starting lineup.

Domantas Sabonis still remains the most well-rounded offensive option on the offense, and Darius Acuff Jr. will have big games with his high usage role, but Keegan Murray is really struggling with his shot this year, and this just isn't an exciting team.

#2647. Landry Shamet has arrived. Why can’t he be Sixth Man of the Year?

Chicken Littles can relax. Our world champion Knicks are 11–6, sit fourth in the Eastern Conference, and have won eight of their last 10 games, including five straight. Karl-Anthony Towns is having an MVP-caliber season, and Captain Jalen Brunson is warming up after a short, celebration-heavy offseason. Another player who's getting some buzz isn't one of the starters, but the team's sharpest weapon off the bench.

When asked about Landry Shamet's play this season, head coach Mike Brown said the 6'5" guard "should be Sixth Man of the Year. It's not close." Mike should know. He has a front-row seat to the Shamet show every night and at every practice.

One stat I take note of is Game Score. John Hollinger designed it to measure a player's box-score production in a single game. Game Score uses a scale that roughly resembles points scored, with 10 considered an average performance and 40 an outstanding one. It rewards scoring, made field goals, rebounds, assists, steals, and blocks. Shot attempts, missed free throws, turnovers, and personal fouls subtract from the total, and offensive rebounds count more than defensive rebounds.

Through 17 games, Shamet has averaged a Game Score of 8.24. That puts him fourth on the team behind Towns (19.83), Brunson (18.66), and OG Anunoby (11.57). Two starters, Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges, rank fifth and sixth at 6.35 and 5.94, respectively.

This season has been a coming out party for Landry. Although primarily a linchpin of the second unit, he has filled in for starters five times this campaign and is averaging 26.9 minutes per game, the second-most of his NBA career. Consider these statistics, all career-best:

11.4 points per game, fourth-best on the team

The only Knick shooting better from deep is Jordan Clarkson (50%), coincidentally the 2020–21 Sixth Man of the Year. And Jordan's attempted only 12 longballs.

When Hart and Bridges have struggled to find the net, plenty of people have beaten the drum for Shamet to replace one of them in the first five. That sounds fine in theory, but consider Mike Brown's perspective. First, there's the harmony of keeping the Villanova brethren together, and who knows what effect a "demotion" for Josh or Kal might have on the locker room? Second, Shamet is Mike's security blanket. If the starters are spinning their wheels, nothing injects energy into the festivities like a Landry pull-up three on the move. The MSG crowd explodes, and you can see his teammates quicken with excitement. Furthermore, Shamet is doing much of his damage against the opponent's backups. That's hardly a fair fight. AND when the score is close and the team needs a bucket, Brown can turn to Captain Clutch, Towns, and his sparkplug Shamet. Even if Landry doesn't start, he sure can finish.

One downer about Landry's success is the ripple effect on the roster. Overshadowed by Shamet's sizzling shooting is the fact that Miles McBride is also shooting a career high from downtown (42%). Deuce was once a first-off-the-bench candidate. Now, with Shamet hitting the three-ball and Tyler Kolek coming into his own as a playmaker (averaging 4.1 assists to 0.6 turnovers in 13.3 minutes per game), McBride is down to 17.2 minutes per night, the fourth-highest average of his six-season career. Meanwhile, the Knicks find themselves dreadfully thin at center, with Andre Drummond losing the plot around the 10-minute mark most nights and James Wiseman yet to prove he can hang. Shamet + Kolek + Drummond + Wiseman = an expendable Deuce. No one here will be surprised if McBride, the longest-tenured Knick, is traded before the deadline for a serviceable big man. No, we won't like it, but we'll understand it.

Consider this: only three Knicks have won Sixth Man of the Year.

Why can't ShamWow be the fourth? He'll have some stiff competition in the race. Boston's Payton Pritchard is the current betting favorite for Sixth Man of the Year (+160 at BetMGM). That vanilla Milk Dud averages 13.7 points per game. Other top contenders include Ajay Mitchell (Thunder), Dylan Harper (Spurs), Jrue Holiday (Blazers), and Ayo Dosunmu (Timberwolves). Jared McCain and Daniss Jenkins are dark horses.

The stats make Landry a strong candidate, though. Through Nov. 22, Shamet ranked fifth in the NBA in on/off net rating among 242 qualifying players on HoopsNightly's leaderboard. The Knicks outscored opponents by 17.2 points per 100 possessions with him on the floor and were outscored by 8.3 with him off it. That's a swing of +25.5. (KnickStats gives him an even better number, +28.)

There used to be two knocks on Shamet, now in his ninth season. The first was that his defense stunk. Well, whattayaknow: according to KnickStats, the Knicks have allowed 101.3 points per 100 possessions with him on the floor and 117.5 with him off it. The other concern was the injury bug. He's missed significant time with lower-body issues, including multiple ankle sprains, a foot injury that kept him out for an extended stretch in 2023, and a calf strain that ended his 2023–24 season. Then came the right-shoulder setbacks, a dislocation in the 2024 preseason and a sprain in 2025 that sidelined him for roughly a month. For now (no jinxes), he's been the picture of health, playing every game of the campaign (we all wince whenever he smashes to the floor).

Everything's good until it isn't again. So it goes. For now, the Knicks are surging and tonight they'll face a familiar rival in the Cleveland Cavaliers. If you saw the injury report, it's a little dicey. Anunoby and Clarkson are out, while Hart, McBride, and Towns are all game-time decisions. That's a concerning list at first blush, but with sixth man Shamet in their back pocket, the Knicks still have a good chance to win their sixth straight. What a time to be a fan.

#2641. Aaron Rodgers: Mike McCarthy fell asleep in meeting last week, broke down Steelers with "1-2-3 Packers"

Aaron Rodgers made his first public comments since being benched by the Steelers on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday afternoon and they were very critical of head coach Mike McCarthy.

Rodgers said he did not hear the news of the quarterback change directly from McCarthy or anyone else on the coaching staff, but got the word from tight end Pat Freiermuth after it was announced on Tuesday night. Rodgers said that the change came after “months of conversation” about the offensive operation, including the playcalling, and that “things went to a different place” in recent days.

Rodgers said that McCarthy fell asleep in an quarterback meeting last Wednesday and missed other meetings leading into their loss to the Eagles on Sunday. Rodgers said McCarthy also broke down the team with “1-2-3 Packers” at halftime of that game and that McCarthy was not regularly watching film while preparing for games. Rodgers said he also believes McCarthy has lost the team in general.

“Everybody in that building knows the truth,” Rodgers said.

Rodgers said similar things happened when the two men were with the Packers and that he believes McCarthy blames him for being fired in Green Bay after the 2018 season. He said he saw that McCarthy was not connecting with Steelers players early in training camp, but tried to help smooth things out.

“I protected him,” Rodgers said. “I didn’t talk about the things publicly. I didn’t talk about his habits.”

Rodgers also said he pushed to have changes made to the playcalling and game-planning that he believed were going to take place before Tuesday’s benching pushed things in a different direction. Rodgers said that he told the team that if they weren’t going to make those alterations that they should release him and said that there was no chance of a reconciliation with the team after how they handled things on Tuesday.

The comments guarantee that Steelers players will be asked for their accounts of how things have been in the building since McCarthy’s arrival this offseason and their responses will likely determine whether or not things go completely off the rails for the team in the final weeks of the season.

#2637. 'It is the only way to be a good team' - Ruben Amorim demands Europa League improvement from injury-hit AC Milan ahead of 'aggressive' Olympiacos trip

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim has laid down the gauntlet to his squad, insisting that finding consistency across both domestic and European competitions is the only path to becoming a truly elite side. The Rossoneri face a daunting trip to Athens to face Olympiacos on Thursday, knowing their recent continental form has been far from the standard expected at San Siro.

Amorim is refusing to let his AC Milan side rest on their laurels following a comprehensive 5-1 thrashing of Frosinone in Serie A. The Portuguese tactician is acutely aware that while domestic results have improved, the club's standing in the Europa League remains precarious, with Milan sitting 28th in the table on just three points.

The manager was blunt about the areas requiring immediate attention as the team prepares for the trip to Athens. 'It's a fact that we need to improve in the final third,' Amorim admitted during his pre-match press conference. 'The only thing we can do is improve our principles. We need to improve on these little things, and that's the only way I can help my players. Against Olympiacos, it will be a different match than the one against Frosinone, just as it will be different than the one against Cagliari. We need to improve, even in our defending. We've almost always conceded a goal, so that's another area we need to improve.'

Milan's European campaign has been a source of frustration this season, characterised by a lack of clinical finishing and defensive lapses. Aside from a lone 4-0 victory over RB Salzburg, the Italian giants have suffered defeats against Bournemouth, Benfica, and Ferencvaros without managing to find the back of the net.

The task ahead is made significantly more difficult by a mounting injury list that has depleted Amorim's options across the pitch. The Rossoneri will be without a host of first-team stars, with Luka Modric, Strahinja Pavlovic, Francesco Camarda, and Davide Bartesaghi the latest names to join the treatment table. They join an already crowded medical room that includes Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Alexis Saelemaekers, and Pietro Terracciano, leaving the squad stretched thin at a critical juncture of the season.

Despite these absences, Amorim refuses to accept the lack of squad depth as a valid reason for failure. 'To be a good team, you have to do well both in the league and in Europe,' he insisted. 'That's the only way to be a good team. We have to be, especially at Milan. I'm always waiting for things to go badly, because it doesn't take much to change the situation. That's what I'm trying to make my players understand, because it won't always be this way. We're at the beginning of a process, and I think we need everyone. We lost Pavlovic, Modric, Saelemaekers, Chukwueze, and everyone has to be ready, because there are no excuses at big clubs. We have to be ready for this. I can't believe we lost all these games in Europe because we rotated.'

Olympiacos represent a stern test for this makeshift Milan side, sitting sixth in the Europa League standings with 10 points from their opening four matches. The Greek side have beaten Jagiellonia, Olympique Marseille and Sparta Prague, while their most recent outing ended in a goalless draw away to Stade Rennais.

The Milan boss offered high praise for the opposition while highlighting the need for his own players to step up in the absence of key starters. 'They're a strong team. They're aggressive, especially at home. I've played here twice, and it was tough for me. I know their coach and what he wants to do. They play compact, positive football, 4-3-3, they change a lot, they rotate, they have Jota, a lot of Portuguese players. They're a strong team, and with their fans there, it'll be a tough match. Chiquinho is a great talent, but very impulsive. I hope he plays well tomorrow, but I hope he still has a great career ahead of him.'

While Europe is the immediate focus, Amorim has not abandoned the club's domestic ambitions. Milan currently sit fourth in the Serie A table with 27 points, five behind leaders Lazio. Despite the challenges of his debut season and the current injury crisis, he remains steadfast in his belief that the Rossoneri can remain in the hunt for the Scudetto. When asked about his stance on the Scudetto race, he was unwavering: 'I haven't changed my mind. This year is difficult, but if we have the chance to fight, we'll do it.'

Several coaches have recently been asked about the release of Grand Theft Auto VI and the amount of time players are devoting to the highly anticipated game, and Amorim made his own preference clear. 'I'd rather my players play that every day rather than scroll through social media,' he remarked. 'Social media, and all that stuff, is very difficult for players, who in any case live with more criticism than I do. After Frosinone, I haven't read anything, because that's how I want to live my life.'

#2634. NBA Week 6 Injury Report: Cameron Boozer to miss at least four weeks; don't panic on Cade Cunningham

The injuries keep stacking up across the league, and this stacked rookie class hasn't been immune from it. Cameron Boozer is set to miss at least four weeks with an ankle injury that will force him to miss a third straight game on Wednesday. This would be a great opportunity for Jerami Grant to step into the starting lineup, but he is slated to be re-evaluated around Dec. 6 after suffering a calf strain.

Kris Murray and Jahmai Mashack have each gotten a start in place of Boozer, so far. Mashack didn't do much in his start and was completely out of the rotation for their last game, while Murray was able to do a little more with his opportunity. Taylor Hendricks and Olivier-Maxence Prosper have also taken on extra minutes off the bench with Boozer, Grant and GG Jackson all sidelined.

It's hard to identify a Grizzlies player that's worth picking up. I'm not really confident in any of them providing consistent value, even if the minutes are there. Feel free to take a chance on one of them, but it may be best to look elsewhere. The good news is if you have any other Memphis rotation players, they should see a bump in usage.

Here are 10 other injury updates from around the league.

The latest news on Nurkić has him being re-evaluated on Friday, so hopefully his return isn't far off. Jaxson Hayes has missed three of Utah's last six games with a left knee strain, and he has started two of the three games he has played during that stretch. Mo Bamba has seen some starts as well, though his last one wasn't nearly as productive as the few before that. Kyle Filipowski had his best game of the season on Monday with 21 points and 12 rebounds after not really being in the rotation before that. When Nurkić returns and gets up to speed, he'll be the team's starting center, so the time to stream any of the other options is coming to a close, though managers shouldn't have much confidence in any of them.

Cunningham missed Tuesday's game against the Magic, which was the second time he missed a game over their last four due to right knee soreness. There's no reason to be alarmed right now, but this is worth keeping an eye on. Daniss Jenkins dished out 10 assists as the primary ball handler. Again, keep an eye on the injury report ahead of their matchup with the Bucks on Friday, but don't panic.

#2628. How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Wolves

Game 7 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Sacramento Kings. My dad was in the family room, having what looked to be some kind of religious experience. 13-year-old me walked in, alarmed and… concerned? He had always been a bit of a curmudgeon, and now here he was, dancing in front of the TV, on the verge of bursting into a full-blown "Sister Act" number. I had never seen this side of him before. Whatever had my dad so enraptured seemed like something I'd like to be a part of myself.

"I'll have what he's having," essentially.

In that game, the Big Ticket, Kevin Garnett, would put up a godly stat line of 32 points, 21 boards, five blocks, and four steals, leading the Minnesota Timberwolves over the Kings with a final score of 83-80. It was pandemonium in the Dooley household.

May 19th, 2004, was the date that I was baptized and purified in the waters of Wolves basketball.

They'd go on to play the Los Angeles Lakers in the Western Conference Finals, and all I really remember from that series was Game 6, with the Wolves down 2-3. My dad and I drove over to my grandma's house off Lake Nokomis in South Minneapolis for a Monday visit and to anxiously watch the most important game of the season.

In my grandma's living room, I sank helplessly in her old reclining sofa chair as Kareem "not Abdul-Jabbar" Rush came off the bench and unconsciously fired away haymaker after haymaker from deep. The man they called K-Rush would hit his first six threes before finally missing late in the fourth when the damage had already been done.

In just six games, the Wolves were sent packing by a relative no-name on a roster full of future Hall of Famers. As someone new to the sport, even I knew that this was almost certainly not on the scouting report. Little did I know at the time, though, that the K-Rushes of the league would turn out to be some of my favorite players. But that night at least, I found K-Rush to be a pretty big jerk.

After learning what it felt like to be punched in the gut by sports – and I must say, it didn't feel great – I was now impatiently waiting for the next season to kick off.

Actually, I was more than ready. The Wolves would be ready as well. I always loved a good story, and the Wolves' was a vengeance quest. They would return. And this time around, they would end up hoisting the trophy that, two weeks later, after the Detroit Pistons shellacked those no-good-dirty-rotten Lakers, I learned belonged to some dude named Larry O'Brien, former NBA commissioner and politician who, according to his Wikipedia page, "learned about politics at a young age."

That hardware was on my mind for the rest of the summer. "Hey, Patrick, wanna go to Sebastian Joe's with me and Sam?" Sorry, can't. Too busy thinking about the Larry O'Brien Trophy.

A female classmate of mine asked me if I wanted to be her boyfriend. After I had just learned about this huge summer event called the NBA draft? Sorry, Ali, I gotta study.

Before I knew it, summer had ended, fall was upon us, and the 2004-05 season was just around the corner. My first full season as a fan of the Minnesota Timberwolves.

The Minnesota Timberwolves join terrifying kids commercials as some of my worst nightmare fuel.

Your teenage years are hard enough as it is. I didn't make it any easier for myself.

I tuned into every game that '04-05 season, waiting for the good vibes to come, but they never did. The January 19th game in Los Angeles against the antagonistic Lakers was an especially nauseating experience. I lay in bed trying to multitask between half-sleeping and listening to Chad Hartman on the radio call. The lights remained on deep into the night. The game was a back-and-forth tilt, with neither team able to get any real separation.

In the end, though, my AM radio would taunt me with Hartman's defeated utterances underneath the static scratches, of missed shots on one end and made shots on the other. Neither were from the right team. It felt unjust. What did I do to deserve this?

Despite running it back, the Wolves just couldn't get over the hump that year, and by proxy, I felt like I couldn't either. This thing called "Wolves fandom" had me feeling sluggish and languid. Like that gut punch from Game 6 of the WCF, I was learning in real time what prolonged, sustained depression feels like. Every game had me on pins and needles. I'm pretty sure this was the year I developed insomnia. I started having frequent sleep paralysis episodes, and also some of the most bizarre nightmares you could imagine.

My dad and I attended the Wolves' final regular-season game that year against the San Antonio Spurs, a team that two months later would be crowned NBA champions. In perhaps their best showing of the season, the Wolves dominated, winning by 22 points.

Former Wolves project Ndudi Ebi had what, to this day, is still the worst airball I have ever seen on a three-point "attempt". He also brought the roof down with a ferocious dunk that had the whole backboard shaking. That was the joy of guys like that.

We were sitting in the lower level right behind the hoop, equal parts in awe and also concerned that we were about to bear witness to a Shaq-shattering-the-backboard moment. (Un)fortunately, that moment never came, and after the game had ended, we left the Target Center wondering what could have been. If they had just played like that all season, maybe things could've gone differently.

Trendy pre-season favorites to win it all, the Wolves missed the playoffs that year, only managing to go 44-38. The late great coach Flip Saunders was fired 51 games into the season, replaced by General Manager and very tall man Kevin McHale.

Little did I know that, over the next 14 years, when my age would double and my stubble would fully grow into a lumberjack beard, at least record-wise, 2005 would be the summit.

The years that followed were a fast, rocky descent down a black diamond, and I was a kid with two left skis, held together with duct tape and blind hope.

Wavering optimism in the circles of Hell, or the life of a Wolves fan.

Sometimes I felt I had made a terrible mistake.

I had unknowingly chained a handcuff I didn't even know I was wearing to a ball dribbled by jesters, malcontents, and egocentrics: Ricky Davis, Marko Jarić, future podcaster Rashad McCants, and some guy with two first names whose scoring was inexplicably halved (20.3 to 10.1) because, as I was starting to realize, the Wolves were a team that could never have nice things.

Dwane Casey was hired as head coach for the 2005-06 season, and then was disposed of a season and a half later. This team was a steaming pile of dung, and the joke was on me for locking myself in the barn, waiting for the heap to turn to roses.

Fast-forward to the summer of '08: "The Dark Knight" had just come out. I went to the Southdale theater to watch the blockbuster film my peers were touting as "the best movie ever", a performance by the late Heath Ledger that critics were lauding as "Oscar-worthy". They weren't wrong. It was quite transformative. I thought to myself, "This was the same guy who played that cowboy?"

Now, I never contemplated becoming the Joker. If it had been released a year earlier, however, I may have considered it.

The previous summer, Garnett had finally had enough and rather unceremoniously parted ways with the Wolves in a big "blockbuster" trade. Minnesota's return really only had two bright spots to note, the first obviously being Al "Big Al" Jefferson.

Defending dunk contest champion Gerald Green.

Under the tutelage of perpetually confused Randy Wittman, the 2007-08 Wolves would go 22-60. Make no mistake, they were god-awful. But during that season's all-star game festivities, something finally clicked for me.

At New Orleans Arena, Gerald Green participated in the Saturday night dunk contest to defend his title, ultimately going toe-to-toe with Dwight Howard, AKA "Superman". Green broke out all sorts of crazy dunks: the alley-oop windmill, a behind-the-backboard under-the-legs slam. But there was one dunk that I will never, ever forget.

The cupcake dunk had never been pulled off, let alone even attempted. It has still not been replicated, nor has anyone, to my knowledge, dared even try.

Though Green would go on to relinquish his title to Howard, that dunk was the talk of the night. And I truly believe the only reason he didn't get a perfect score on it was because the judges didn't see what we all saw.

And it got me thinking. On a rudderless team, both managed and saddled by an inept franchise, what else is there to see? What can I look for?

To start, I accepted the truth: this team wasn't winning anything anytime soon.

Now that actual expectations had been tabled, I could watch the Wolves without worrying about superfluous things like "the outcome of a game" or "where the Wolves sit in the standings". If they lost, well, that's okay. I expected them to. If they won, I was amused. I had even perfected my dad's patented half-smile.

I also became a more well-rounded basketball fan, always following a second team to supplement my thirst for promising development. After the Seattle SuperSonics moved to Oklahoma City in 2008, I started to follow the young upstart Thunder. Making the leap from 23 wins to 50 in just one year. As a Wolves fan, I could've felt envy, but instead I was like a proud stepfather. I was the fan that stepped up.

In 2012, when they made it all the way to the Finals only to lose to that villainous Miami Heat superteam, I took it personally. But it felt good to care. The stakes had never been higher. I could never feel that way about the Wolves, who were in a league of their own.

And I tried to see it all for what it was: just basketball. Like the Actor in Albert Camus' "The Myth of Sisyphus", I invested myself in the Wolves for two-ish hours every game night, and once the contest was over, it was back to business as usual. It was back to life as usual. I wouldn't let the Wolves define me. They wouldn't determine how I felt moving forward. Sometimes a game would end in heartbreaking fashion, and I would feel that tiny hammer starting to peck away at that thing in my chest. No. I would relent. I refuse to let it hurt.

Well, if I was built like this guy, this would have been way easier.

But eventually I had to interrogate something deep: Why did I start following this team in the first place?

I had chosen to attach myself to this team during some of the most formative years of my life. And despite the Wolves at times almost insisting that I leave them be, I could never.

My father has lived in Minneapolis his entire life. As have I. I guess you could say we are predisposed to Minnesota sports fandom. It's in our bloodstream. When I watched my father react so fervently to that epic Game 7 all those years ago, it felt like something I would like to share with him. Up to that point, we hadn't shared all that much.

That shared fandom extends far beyond the father-son bond. It's a communal thing. Minneapolis is Wolves territory. To have pride in them is just one of the ways I choose to have pride in my community, where I'm from and where I stay to this day.

In 2013, having just graduated from the University of St. Thomas, I discovered Canis Hoopus, another communal outlet for me to share my allegiance to Wolves basketball. That became a way for me to lean into the real truth I had been avoiding. Like it or not, the Wolves were now an integral part of me. And to ignore that part, to detach myself from it and let myself become jaded would, as Camus so bluntly put it, be a defeat of the human soul.

So, whether I was using Canis to spam the game threads with Free Dieng! or as an excuse to play around with iMovie, I was no longer afraid to let it all out. The Wolves were like an alley-oop, and I was Gerald Green, or Zach LaVine – take your pick; if there's one thing the Wolves have, it's dunk champs – and the team was all of us, together.

Not too long after Garnett was traded, another movie came out: "Into the Wild", adapted from the novel of the same name and the real-life story of Christopher McCandless, a naive, pretentious young college graduate who, left to his own devices, went on a solo hike across North America and into the Alaskan wilderness. Along the way, he made many friends, but ultimately always left them behind to continue his trek alone.

Eventually, he ate a berry that turned out to be poisonous. He would soon pass away in an abandoned bus in the wild, but not before writing in his journal a revelatory "Happiness is only real when shared."

While I find that a bit reductive, I believe that happiness is best when shared. And it's not just limited to happiness. As my former neighbor Dave Pirner once sang, "Misery loves company."

The highs and the lows, the celebratory and the funereal. All of it is best, and can be eased, by a shared camaraderie among people.

And that's how I learned to truly embrace the Wolves, by finding community in the struggle, and by finding myself in that communal openness where all mirrors are welcome, where the subjective woe can turn into a collective joy, and I am forever grateful for that.

#2623. Rob Pelinka believes the Lakers are feeding off Luka Dončić’s leadership

Behind Luka Dončić's wondrous play, which has thrust him into the center of early season MVP conversations, the Los Angeles Lakers are off to a roaring 15-3 start and tied for the West's No. 1 seed. Whether it's his elite self-creation, willingness to embrace more off-ball work, brilliant playmaking or growth on the defensive end, there are many on-court factors explaining why Dončić has been so impactful for Los Angeles this year.

But Lakers GM Rob Pelinka also believes Dončić's leadership is paramount to this team's success thus far. Pelinka deems Dončić's leadership as bred through plenty of personal experiences that have shaped him in recent years.

"Adversity in life is what makes us all grow and he's been through a lot. Getting traded, he's had some family stuff, making sure he can stay close to his daughters," Pelinka said prior to Friday's win over the Sacramento Kings. "That's all adversity and I've seen it really grow his character in the form of leadership just being able to go through some of that stuff that life throws all of us, it throws our way. The guys in the locker room feed off his leadership. The other thing I've really seen about Luka is he takes accountability. He has so many great games but if he has a down game, he looks around the guys, he's like, 'This one's on me. I've got to be better.' I think a great leader can recognize that and really have seen that growth in him this year."

Pelinka's mention of accountability was readily on display last week when the Lakers' nine-game winning streak came to a halt after they lost to the Utah Jazz. That night, Dončić scored 29 points on 10-of-28 shooting (2-of-12 from deep) and had seven assists to nine turnovers. Following the defeat, Dončić didn't mince words about his own play and refused to let the second leg of a back-to-back be any sort of excuse for the team's poor performance.

"I mean, honestly, I just got to be way better than this," Dončić told reporters. "This is unacceptable for my part. I've got to lead the team in better ways. I look at this game, got to move on and learn from this."

The Lakers will hope both Dončić's leadership and on-court splendor power them to a win Friday night when they face the San Antonio Spurs in a clash between 15-3 teams vying for the West's top spot.

#2618. Joe Brady can become the fifth coach ever to win 10 of his first 11 games

Buffalo’s Joe Brady is off to one of the best starts for any head coach in NFL history.

The Bills are 9-1, which means that if they beat the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, Brady will be just the fifth coach in NFL history to win 10 of his first 11 games.

The four who have done it before are Jim Caldwell (11-0 with the 2009 Colts), Wally Lemm (who went 9-0 as interim head coach of the 1961 Houston Oilers and then won one of his first two games after becoming head coach of the 1962 St. Louis Cardinals), Steve Mariucci (10-1 with the 1997 49ers) and Red Miller (10-1 with the 1977 Broncos).

Brady took over a good Bills team and has kept them near the top of the NFL. His record to start his head-coaching career is impressive, but he was brought in to win in the postseason, and so it’s too soon to say whether the Bills’ decision to fire Sean McDermott and replace him with Brady will pay off.

#2610. NFL Thanksgiving DFS Picks and Player Props: Best Week 12 Bets and Lineup Strategy

Thanksgiving week gives us five NFL games before Sunday, which means plenty of opportunities to have a little extra interest in the holiday slate. Kyle Soppe and I went through his favorite DFS angles and the player props we're targeting across the Wednesday night, Thanksgiving, and Black Friday games.

The three-game Thanksgiving DFS slate is especially interesting because there are only six teams to choose from. That makes differentiation more important than it would be on a normal Sunday, when managers can spread exposure across eight or 10 games. On the betting side, I'm primarily looking for player props where the market hasn't fully accounted for role, matchup, or expected game script.

All betting lines and prices referenced below are from the time of recording and are subject to change.

Soppe wants to build around Detroit against Chicago, but not in the most obvious way. His core stack is Jared Goff with Jameson Williams and Sam LaPorta, intentionally leaving out Amon-Ra St. Brown to create a lineup that looks different from the likely Goff-St. Brown combinations across the field.

The theory is straightforward. If Williams hits another long touchdown, Goff gets the same production without St. Brown contributing anything to that drive. Chicago has been vulnerable to vertical passing, which aligns perfectly with Williams' role, and his explosive-play profile gives the stack a chance to separate quickly.

LaPorta provides a different path. Soppe isn't projecting eight catches and 100 yards, but he has continued to draw meaningful red-zone opportunities. Four or five catches plus a touchdown would be enough for him to pay off while still giving Goff another way to post a tournament-winning score.

If Soppe is fading St. Brown, he wants to spend his premium wide receiver salary on CeeDee Lamb. Lamb has consistently drawn heavy volume against Philadelphia, and his role in Dallas' offense remains considerably more stable than most of the other expensive options on the slate.

George Pickens may draw more attention after consecutive 100-yard games and four touchdowns over that stretch. That discount is tempting, but Soppe doesn't think the gap in salary accurately reflects the gap in role and consistency. Lamb becomes the tournament pivot if more lineups gravitate toward Pickens.

Khalil Shakir is another player Soppe wants exposure to against Kansas City. The Chiefs have done an excellent job limiting opponents downfield, which naturally funnels throws toward the shorter areas where Shakir operates.

START PREPARING: PFN's FREE Fantasy Draft Simulator

He has also caught at least six passes in four straight meetings with Kansas City. Shakir is coming off his first 100-yard game of the season, and his ability after the catch gives him more upside than his shallow target profile might initially suggest. Five or six receptions can turn into a much bigger DFS performance if he creates something after the catch.

The Cowboys defense is the part of Soppe's lineup that nobody is going to feel good about. Dallas has been one of the league's worst defenses, and the Cowboys are also expensive enough that most DFS players will naturally gravitate elsewhere.

That's exactly why Soppe is interested. Philadelphia is starting Joe Milton, and the expected game script could force him into 30-plus dropbacks if Dallas builds a sizable lead. Even a bad defense can create sacks and turnovers when an inexperienced quarterback has to repeatedly throw from behind.

Soppe isn't suddenly arguing that Dallas has become a good defense. This is a tournament play built around low ownership and a specific game script. If Milton is forced into obvious passing situations for most of the second half, the Cowboys have a path to a score that very few opposing DFS lineups will own.

My first play is Joe Milton over 26.5 rushing yards. I grabbed the number early, and it had already climbed into the low 30s by the time we recorded, but I was still willing to play it around 32.5.

Milton ran effectively in his first start before Philadelphia unexpectedly played from ahead against Pittsburgh in Week 11. That limited him to around 20 dropbacks and only a handful of rushing opportunities. I don't expect the same game script against Dallas.

If Philadelphia trails, Milton should have considerably more opportunities to scramble. Dallas has already allowed meaningful rushing production to mobile quarterbacks, and Soppe also likes the possibility of Milton picking up yards in softer late-game coverage if the Cowboys build a lead.

Soppe's Eagles prop is Mekhi Lemon to catch at least four passes. Dallas has allowed opponents to complete a very high percentage of short throws, and Lemon doesn't need to do anything spectacular with those opportunities for this bet to cash.

We're looking for volume more than explosiveness. If Milton gives Lemon six or seven short targets in negative game script, four catches is a reasonable expectation even if the final yardage total doesn't impress anyone.

I'm going back to Jordan Love over 1.5 passing touchdowns against the Rams. He has thrown multiple touchdowns in all but two games this season, and Green Bay's current backfield situation gives me even more reason to expect the offense to run through him.

Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play, and the Packers have struggled to generate efficient rushing production without him. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden give Love multiple ways to create explosive plays, while Tucker Kraft can provide another option closer to the goal line.

This doesn't require Green Bay to light up the Rams for 35 points. I simply need two of its scoring drives to end through the air rather than on the ground, and that's a wager I'm willing to make at close to even money.

Soppe is taking the other side of the overall offensive enthusiasm with the Packers-Rams game total under 44.5. Those two positions don't necessarily conflict. Love can throw two touchdowns in a 23-17 game and both bets get there.

FANTASY RANKINGS: PFN's FREE Fantasy PPR, Half-PPR, and Non-PPR Rankings

Los Angeles is the larger reason for the under. The Rams are without their top receiving options and have every incentive to lean on Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, shortening the game in the process. Soppe sees enough reasons for both offenses to play methodically that he's willing to bet against a shootout.

Caleb Williams over 32.5 pass attempts is one of my favorite Thanksgiving angles. He had cleared this number in four consecutive games before Chicago controlled the Saints throughout Week 11 and didn't need him to throw nearly as much.

Detroit presents a completely different environment. The Lions are difficult to run against, while the Bears are coming off a game in which D'Andre Swift lost another fumble and Kyle Monangai managed 18 yards on 10 carries. I expect Ben Johnson to put more of the game in Williams' hands.

The opponent helps as well. Detroit can score enough to force Chicago to remain aggressive for four quarters, and Johnson knows the Lions personnel better than almost anyone. The line had moved to 33.5 at some books by the time of recording, and I was still comfortable playing the over there.

This is not the glamorous bet of the Thanksgiving slate. Brock Wright over 3.5 receiving yards is essentially a wager that he catches one normal NFL pass.

Wright has been on the field more frequently recently, including a 74% snap share in Week 11, and he ran 14 routes in that game. His receptions prop was considerably more expensive than the yardage bet, so I'd rather take the receiving yards and trust that one catch gets us there.

Soppe floated the idea of getting aggressive and laddering Wright all the way to 15 yards at plus money. I am not turning Brock Wright into the centerpiece of my Thanksgiving betting card, but I understand the logic given his career yards per reception.

Soppe is expecting Bears-Lions to become one of the day's more entertaining games, but he's betting on a slower start with under 10.5 first-quarter points. Detroit has not been especially productive on a per-drive basis in the opening quarter, while both defenses have performed relatively well early in games.

We aren't betting against the offenses for the full 60 minutes. A 7-3 or 3-3 first quarter gets the job done, and there is still plenty of time afterward for the game to develop into the back-and-forth environment both of us expect.

Josh Downs is another player whose role I expect to grow on Thanksgiving night. His snap share went from 17% in his Chiefs debut to 23% in his second game, but Kansas City won both games comfortably enough that it had no reason to rush him into a full-time role.

Buffalo should require more. I think Downs can push toward a 50% snap share in a competitive game, and the potential for difficult weather could actually work in his favor because his routes are concentrated closer to the line of scrimmage.

Downs has already caught four passes in each of his first two games despite the limited playing time. Give him a larger role against Buffalo and I like his chances to reach four again.

Soppe prefers Shakir to catch more passes than Downs, which created our own little Thanksgiving debate. Shakir has the more established role and has repeatedly produced six-catch games against Kansas City, while I'm expecting Downs' playing time to expand dramatically.

My hesitation with Shakir is Dalton Kincaid's potential return. Shakir's role has sometimes benefited when Buffalo's other short-area options are unavailable, while Downs could be trending in the opposite direction as Kansas City integrates him further into the offense.

That isn't one of my official wagers from the slate, but it captures the difference between our projections. Soppe trusts Shakir's established volume; I'm betting on Downs' role expanding.

My Black Friday card starts with Jonah Coleman under 18.5 rushing attempts. Coleman handled 24 carries and 28 total touches against Las Vegas on Sunday, and now Denver is asking a rookie running back to come back five days later against Pittsburgh.

I still love Coleman for fantasy. The under isn't a statement that he loses his lead role or struggles in the game. I simply don't expect Sean Payton to immediately give him another 20-plus carries on short rest.

Pittsburgh should also provide more resistance than Las Vegas did. A more competitive game with fewer sustained Denver drives gives Coleman a realistic path to 15 or 16 carries while still producing a perfectly useful fantasy performance.

Jaylen Warren over 2.5 receptions is the first of several Pittsburgh overs I'm playing. Warren has caught at least three passes in six of 10 games, while Denver has consistently allowed running backs to contribute as receivers.

That includes multiple opposing backfields producing three-catch players in recent weeks. Denver's pressure also creates natural opportunities for Aaron Rodgers to get the ball out quickly, and Warren remains Pittsburgh's preferred receiving back despite Rico Dowdle's presence.

I'm attacking Pittsburgh's extremely low receiving-yardage lines rather than betting Rodgers to have a big passing game. The three numbers I played were Darnell Washington over 18.5 receiving yards, Pat Freiermuth over 19.5, and Roman Wilson over 17.5.

Denver has been vulnerable to tight ends, which gives me enough reason to take both Washington and Freiermuth at such low thresholds. I'm not trying to predict which one produces the better fantasy game. I just think Rodgers can distribute enough yardage for both to reach roughly 20.

Wilson's number is appealing for the same reason. He can clear 17.5 yards on one reception, and I don't expect Michael Pittman's return to completely erase him from the offense. Jeremy Bernard also saw 10 targets last week, leaving Pittsburgh with enough moving parts that the receiving production can be spread around.

Soppe's primary concern is DK Metcalf hitting one huge play and consuming too much of Rodgers' limited passing total. That's the clearest way this group of overs fails together. My bet is that Rodgers continues spreading the ball around enough for at least the majority of these extremely low numbers to cash.

The condensed slate requires a slightly different approach on both sides. In DFS, Soppe is looking for ways to tell a coherent game story without simply duplicating the most obvious lineup in the field. That's why his Detroit stack leaves out St. Brown and why he's willing to use a bad Cowboys defense in a potentially favorable game script.

My prop card is built more around role and thresholds. Williams' passing volume, Downs' increasing involvement, Warren's receiving work, and the low Pittsburgh receiving totals all give me opportunities where I think the number matters more than projecting a massive individual performance.

There is a lot of football before Sunday, so I don't love the idea of chasing losses if the early games go badly. The goal is the same as it is every week: Find the numbers that are worth betting, accept that some won't hit, and don't turn a holiday slate into an excuse to force action on every game.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

#2609. Kevin Porter Jr. reportedly finalizing 2-year deal with Magic

Kevin Porter Jr. is finally on a team for the 2026-27 NBA season. A month after being waived by the Milwaukee Bucks, Porter will reportedly sign a two-year deal with the Orlando Magic, per ESPN.

Porter, 26, underwent knee surgery in April and was waived by the Bucks just days before the first game of the regular season.

Porter — whose 2025-26 season was delayed due to a knee injury — was out to a great start with the Bucks last season, averaging 17.4 points and 7.4 assists. But he was limited to just 38 games after sustaining another knee injury, this one forcing him to undergo surgery in April.

Porter picked up a player option to remain with the Bucks and was able to take part in Milwaukee's training camp. He appeared in the team's preseason game against the Indiana Pacers just prior to his release, scoring 11 points in 15 minutes.

Despite proving he was healthy, Porter remained on the free-agent market for over a month before reportedly joining the Magic. He also met with the Denver Nuggets during the season.

Once he signs, Porter will join his fifth NBA team since being drafted in the first round of the 2019 NBA Draft.

Porter has had some off-the-court issues that have contributed to his vagabond NBA journey, most notably pleading guilty to misdemeanor assault and a harassment violation in New York in 2024 in a case involving former girlfriend and ex-WNBA player Kysre Gondrezick.

#2605. Pat McAfee floored by Aaron Rodgers remarks about ‘unhealthy’ Mike McCarthy that got him cut

Pat McAfee was completely stunned while Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers unleashed some serious allegations against his now former head coach Mike McCarthy on Wednesday.

The four-time NFL MVP appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" after the Steelers announced Tuesday night he would be inactive for Friday's game against the Broncos and replaced by Mason Rudolph.

McAfee's jaw dropped when Rodgers claimed he confronted McCarthy about the coach sleeping and snoring during team meetings and missing walk-throughs — adding that it's allegedly a known behavioral pattern exhibited by McCarthy in the Steelers' building.

Pat McAfee reacts to Aaron Rodgers discussing his issues with the Steelers on his show, Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. X

The Steelers released Rodgers shortly after he went scorched earth on-air.

Rodgers explained that "the nail in the coffin" occurred during Pittsburgh's 19-16 loss to the Eagles, when McCarthy purportedly broke up the halftime huddle by saying, "1-2-3 Packers."

"'1-2-3 Packers' is crazy," Rodgers said. "On the bus and in all of our group chats it was talked about, like how was that possible."

McCarthy coached Rodgers with the Packers from 2006 through December 2018 and they won a Super Bowl by beating the Steelers to cap the 2010 season.

Rodgers claimed things have been contentious behind the scenes for months — and that the team thought there needed to be a change with the offense because of McCarthy.

He explained that he confronted McCarthy as a "concerned friend" because he believed the coach was "unhealthy" due to him allegedly dozing off in meetings.

Rodgers said he found out he was going to be inactive from tight end Pat Freiermuth on a phone call Tuesday night, and that being benched was never a discussion with McCarthy.

"I'm standing on the truth, that's why it's not emotional for me anymore," Rodgers said. "Everyone knows it and everyone talks about it all over the building."

The 42-year-old signal-caller challenged the Steelers to release him if changes weren't implemented — and they took him up on his offer after his shocking interview.

Aaron Rodgers discussing his issues with the Steelers during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show," Nov. 25, 2026. X

"Obviously the team has chosen to back Mike," Rodgers said before his release. "We know where the players stand. Not even a question."

He also accused the franchise of trying to spin a narrative of benching him to steer the attention away from McCarthy's alleged issues.

McAfee was visibly taken aback by Rodgers spilling the tea on what's allegedly happening behind the scenes in Pittsburgh.

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) talks with head coach Mike McCarthy during an NFL game on Sept. 27, 2026, at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect

"At training camp when we were up there it felt good … Mike McCarthy coming back to [coach in] his hometown," McAfee said, noting that "after the bye week [Week 9] it feels like things have gotten a bit different."

Rodgers and McCarthy had a heated exchange that was caught on a hot mic during a 27-24 loss to the Browns in Week 4 when the quarterback became upset during the first quarter of the Thursday game while waiting for his longtime coach to make a play call.

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) reacts after a game at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

A Prime Video mic picked up Rodgers yelling, "What the f–k? Call it!" while looking at McCarthy on the sideline.

Rodgers, who turns 43 next week, returned to Pittsburgh on a one-year, $22.5 million contract for what he said will be his final NFL season.

He told McAfee that he felt responsible for the Steelers' issues because he vouched for McCarthy's hire in Pittsburgh, which happened in January.

The Steelers are 6-4 heading into Friday's game against Denver.

It's possible that Rodgers has now potentially played in the last game of his career.

#2599. Why was Amad Diallo’s equaliser against Sporting disallowed?

Manchester United were furious as Amad Diallo's equaliser against Sporting was disallowed for a foul in the build-up.

Referee Szymon Marciniak ruled that Youri Tielemans had committed a foul on Goncalo Inacio when he slid to poke the ball through to Amad.

The United winger saw his shot saved by Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira but he followed in to head the ball into an empty net.

Sporting v Man United LIVE: Latest Champions League score and updates

The goal could not be reviewed because the referee had already given a foul (PA)

However, because Marciniak had already blown his whistle to stop play following the challenge from Tielemans, VAR could not intervene.

Tielemans did not appear to commit a foul and instead won the ball fairly against Inacio when he went to ground to play the ball through to Amad.

Tielemans was also booked by Marciniak, who took charge of the 2022 World Cup final, for protesting.

"It was a dreadful decision," former United midfielder Owen Hargreaves said on TNT Sports. "I don't know what [the referee] saw. [Tielemans] played the ball. It wasn't reckless."

Manchester United's Youri Tielemans remonstrates with referee Szymon Marciniak (Reuters)

It came after Mauricio Pochettino saw his new defence concede two penalties in the space of three minutes in a shambolic first-half spell.

The hosts received the chance to open the scoring when Lisandro Martinez was ruled to have fouled winger Geny Catamo by catching him with an outstretched leg.

If it appeared soft, justice was perhaps served when Senne Lammens saved a tame effort from Sporting striker Luis Suarez low down to his left.

But in farcical scenes, Lammens then conceded another penalty just 75 seconds later when he crashed into Maximiliano Araujo in the box.

Suarez took the second penalty and made no mistake to give Sporting the lead, as United conceded the opening goal for the seventh match in a row.

It was the first time United had conceded two penalties in the same Champions League match since 1998, while they have now conceded five in total in all competitions this season.

#2596. Best Aaron Rodgers landing spots after Steelers cut ties with star QB

The Pittsburgh Steelers have reportedly cut ties with quarterback Aaron Rodgers and now it'll be interesting to see if he ends up with another team the rest of the season.

The move comes in the wake of Rodgers getting benched on Tuesday and ripping head coach Mike McCarthy to shreds on Wednesday during an interview on "The Pat McAfee Show."

Following Rodgers' interview with McAfee, it was reported that the Steelers are cutting the future Hall of Famer, who will now go to waivers.

MORE: Steelers must fire Mike McCarthy amid Aaron Rodgers fiasco

If nobody claims Rodgers, he will be free to sign with any team, assuming he plans to continue playing in what Rodgers said would be his final season in the NFL.

If Rodgers does end up hitting free agency, he's going to want to play for a team that at least has a chance to make the playoffs. Here's three teams that fit the bill and could also look to add a quarterback between now and the weeks ahead.

Football – NFL – New England Patriots Press Conference – Munich, Germany – November 13, 2026 New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel during the press conference REUTERS/Angelika Warmuth Credit: REUTERS (Reuters)

This is the one that makes the most sense.

The Patriots lost Drake Maye for the rest of the season and now their hopes rest on the arm of backup Tommy DeVito, who has shown he isn't going to keep this team afloat.

At 5-5, the Patriots are still alive in the playoff race and are just one game behind both the Cleveland Browns and Steelers for the No. 6 and 7 spots.

Rodgers would definitely be an upgrade over DeVito and could save New England's season.

New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh reacts during the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

After losing Jaxson Dart for the rest of the season, the Giants traded for J.J. McCarthy, who has since replaced the struggling Jameis Winston.

While McCarthy has looked better than he did during his Minnesota Vikings stint and is 3-1 as the starter, his play hasn't exactly been great and there is room for improvement.

Rodgers could be that improvement if he signs with New York, and if he can elevate the offense there, the first-place Giants could make a serious run.

Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken looks on during the first half against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

While Deshaun Watson has certainly been better this season than he was in years past, that bar is incredibly low and there's no question things can be better in Cleveland.

Despite Watson's improved play, the Browns still rank in the bottom half of the NFL in passing yards per game and 27th in points scored.

If Watson starts to struggle in the next few weeks and the Browns, who are sitting in the No. 6 playoff spot currently, begin to see their playoff hopes slip, they might consider Rodgers.

Unfortunately, there would be no Rodgers vs. Steelers showdown if he signs with the Browns, as the Browns and Steelers have already played twice this season.

#2595. 49ers get a Brock Purdy injury scare with Seahawks looming

The San Francisco 49ers had some unexpected news Wednesday as they began their preparation for Sunday's game against the rival Seattle Seahawks.

Quarterback Brock Purdy missed Wednesday's practice due to an ankle injury he suffered in the second quarter of Sunday's 35-10 victory over the Minnesota Vikings, head coach Kyle Shanahan said.

San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (13) throws a pass against the Dallas Cowboys in Arlington, Texas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

The injury puts Purdy's status in question ahead of Sunday's game as the 49ers look to take a stranglehold of the NFC West. They're 9-1 and enter the weekend with a three-game lead over the second-place Seahawks with a chance to win the head-to-head tiebreaker with six games remaining.

"We'll see. He can't go today," Shanahan said before practice.

San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy reacts before an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AFP via Getty Images

Shanahan said he knew Purdy was hurt from the training staff, who cleared him to stay in the game.

"They always tell you when someone has something," Shanahan said. "But then they came back and said, 'Yeah, he checked out, he should be fine.'"

Purdy played the second half with his ankles taped while the 49ers pulled away from the Vikings' top-ranked defense in Mexico City. Purdy completed 21 of 26 for 255 yards and 3 touchdowns, strengthening his case for MVP candidacy.

San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (13) warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Getty Images

Purdy earned NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors for the fourth time in his career. His 146.0 passer rating against Minnesota marked the seventh time he's posted a rating of at least 145, the most by any quarterback in his first five NFL seasons.

Purdy's ability to sidestep pressure and keep his eyes downfield buys receivers time to uncover, an edge San Francisco could lose if his ankle limits him against Seattle.

If Purdy can't play Sunday, the 49ers would turn to Mac Jones, who kept San Francisco's season afloat in 2025 when Purdy missed eight games with a turf toe injury. The 49ers went 5-3 in Jones' starts while finishing the season 12-5.

They were in the mix for the No. 1 seed all the way until the regular season finale when they lost to Seattle, who also beat the 49ers in the Divisional Round of the playoffs to end their season.

#2594. Where the Dallas Mavericks stand in the NBA cup

After Tuesday night's win over the Denver Nuggets, the Dallas Mavericks are in great position to play for the third annual NBA cup.

The Mavericks are 3-0 in group play, with a point differential of 36, by far the highest in their group.

They also hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Denver Nuggets and Houston Rockets. The only team that could jump the Mavericks is the Phoenix Suns, who play the Rockets tonight, and the Mavericks on Thursday.

With a Rockets win, the Suns would be eliminated from contention, and the Mavericks would be in regardless of Friday's result.

If they do advance to the tournament, it would mean a matchup against another western conference contender. This would give the Mavericks another opportunity to show their mettle, and establish themselves as a real threat within the West.

"It means a lot," said Caleb Martin in his post-game interview with Jeff Wade. "Just to have an oppurtunity to play in these types of enviroments… to test where we're at."

While the NBA cup isn't the same as real playoff basketball, it's much closer than the regular season.

It would be especially helpful for a young Mavericks team that has limited experience in the postseason; Cooper Flagg being the player with the most to gain.

And for those questioning the value of cup games, look no further than last year's Cup final, which featured the eventual NBA finals matchup.

It also gives the Mavericks a chance at redemption for their recent 3-game losing streak against other contending teams, and gives them a chance to add more proverbial skins on the wall.

Their seeding within the tournament will come down to Friday's game against the Suns, but they will likely have a home game in the quarterfinal due to their record and point differential.

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2591. Philip Rivers Hires Former Panthers Star As NC State Coach

Philip Rivers has hired a former Panthers wide receiver to join his new coaching staff at NC State. This move marks a key step for the program as it looks to rebuild under a first-time head coach. The hiring comes just two weeks after Rivers took the reins of the team.

The quarterback has no prior college coaching experience, yet he is already shaping the program's culture. He spent his first week trying to stay out of the way while the interim staff worked. Interim coach Todd Goebbel and his team are still chasing bowl eligibility in the final game against rival North Carolina. Rivers watches players and practice sessions from the edge. He keeps his distance from the game plan while he learns the ropes.

Rivers started 51 games for NC State and remains the most decorated quarterback in school history. Now 44 years old, he will lead the team in 2027.

Rivers is building his staff by looking for the right fit rather than rushing the process. The search for the perfect fit continues as the season winds down.

Rivers has deliberately held off on that approach to see what works for his team. "I kind of have taken the approach of, let me form a little bit of my own opinion and feel this thing out early, and then it's like, 'Huh, I wonder what they did here,' you know?" Rivers said. This method lets him learn the system before making big changes.

The new coach joins a staff that values the quiet moments that build trust. Rivers remembers how his former NFL coach, Norv Turner, would check on players early in the morning. At 5:30 a.m. holding coffee, Turner remained a constant presence in the Chargers' training room. He would check on players and join their idle chatter to build a bond. Rivers sees those same days as crucial for any team, regardless of their record. "Hey, man, these are the days. These are the days, whether you're 4-6 or 10-0. These are the days you're near your guys," Rivers told CBS Sports.

The NC State football team faces its final test this week to secure a bowl berth. The game against North Carolina will determine if the interim staff can finish the season strong. Rivers and his new staff will watch closely before taking full control in 2027.

#2589. NBA plans to invest 10bn euros in European arenas

The NBA has stepped up its plans for a European league by announcing a strategy to invest at least 10bn euros in the development and renovation of basketball arenas across the continent.

The league has assembled a group of investment firms for the project, which would also look to improve the sports and entertainment districts around the arenas.

The initiative forms part of the NBA and the International Basketball Federation's (Fiba) plan to launch a new, professional basketball system in Europe in 2027.

It will provide prospective clubs and ownership groups with access to capital and the NBA's expertise in regard to developing modern arenas and their surroundings.

"We've seen first-hand how state-of-the-art arenas and the related developments around them can transform basketball teams and their surrounding communities," said NBA commissioner Adam Silver.

"As we prepare to launch a new league in Europe alongside Fiba, we see a significant opportunity to help clubs develop facilities which both build on the unique traditions that define European basketball while also elevating the fan experience and attracting many more live events."

The NBA's announcement stated that the plans for the areas surrounding arenas could include housing, workplaces, restaurants, retail and public spaces, ensuring they would be year-round destinations.

In the statement, the investors said: "We're excited to work with the NBA to support a transformative phase of infrastructure development across Europe.

"Together, we have the potential to invest billions of euros to create world-class venues in European cities, honouring the passion and traditions of European basketball fans and supporting lasting economic growth in the communities where the game means so much."

The announcement cited a study by The Sports Consultancy, which claimed the NBA and Fiba's league could contribute more than 24bn euros in gross value added to GDP across Europe.

It also claimed the league could support nearly 15,000 full-time equivalent jobs annually and attract nearly 70 million spectators over its first 10 years.
