#2588. Trent McDuffie reveals how Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald could help him haunt Packers

Trent McDuffie was standing on the sideline of Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland, when he first saw Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald play alongside each other.

The duo, which has five NFL Defensive Player of the Year awards between them, wreaked havoc on the Commanders' offensive line, with Garrett sacking quarterback Jayden Daniels three times in his return from knee surgery.

McDuffie couldn't help but smile as he watched.

Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald (99) greets defensive end Myles Garrett (95) during an NFL game in Landover, Md., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough

It wasn't because the Rams cornerback was enjoying watching the two defensive stars from the sideline but because he was imagining what it would be like to play behind them.

"I couldn't stop smiling on the sideline. Just seeing how aggressive and violent the D-line was attacking," McDuffie told the California Post in an exclusive interview. "As a DB, knowing that I have him up front, it just tells me I have more plays and more opportunities to go make game-changing plays."

McDuffie's first experience playing behind Garrett and Donald in the same game came in LA's 34-6 victory over the Cardinals. The Rams' defense recorded five sacks, two turnovers, and held its NFC West rivals to six points.

Now they'll need to replicate that performance when they face a much different challenge in the Packers on Thanksgiving Eve with the stakes considerably higher.

Los Angeles Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie (22) sits on the NFL Network set during a joint practice against the Dallas Cowboys at the Rams Practice Facility in Woodland Hills, Calif., Tuesday, Aug. 11, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Both teams enter at 6-4, with the winner of Wednesday's matchup gaining a crucial head-to-head tiebreaker in the NFC wild-card race.

The Rams have won four consecutive games, and despite being without defensive tackle Poona Ford and cornerback Jaylen Watson for the remainder of the season, they are finally beginning to resemble the formidable unit they envisioned when they acquired Garrett and McDuffie and lured Donald out of retirement.

"There hasn't been a game yet where really everybody was out there playing together," McDuffie said.

Los Angeles Rams Kobie Turner (91) celebrates a sack against the Detroit Lions during the third quarter of an NFL football game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif., Sunday, Dec. 14, 2025. Getty Images

Kobie Turner was activated off injured reserve ahead of the Thanksgiving Eve matchup with the Packers, and the world will finally have an opportunity to see what the Rams' defense looks like when McDuffie's coverage ability meets the Rams' pass rush at full strength, featuring two of the NFL's most feared defensive players.

"It should be really exciting," McDuffie said. "I think, as a defense, we have a really good opportunity. Just getting another game that we can all play together."

McDuffie's presence could be especially important against Packers quarterback Jordan Love, who will have considerably less time to find open receivers if Garrett and Donald are collapsing the pocket.

And with the Rams missing Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and center Coleman Shelton, the defense may have to do more than keep Green Bay's offense in check.

It may have to carry Los Angeles to victory.

#2585. Lakers star divulges ‘uncomfortable’ reason for success without Austin Reaves

For the first four weeks of the season, the Lakers, for the most part, won their games in similar fashion.

A scorching start from Luka Doncic en route to a 30-point (and oftentimes, 40-point) performance.

Austin Reaves, Doncic's backcourt co-star, efficiently filled in the gaps offensively en route to an uber-efficient 25-point game.

Walker Kessler provided the rim pressure the team needed, which in combination with the scoring/playmaking from Doncic and Reaves, opened up scoring opportunities for the players around them.

Luka Doncic #77 and Austin Reaves #15 of the Los Angeles Lakers look on. NBAE via Getty Images

Los Angeles Lakers forward Jarred Vanderbilt playing defense. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong

The recipe not only led to the Lakers winning 12 of their first 14 games, but also powered them to have the league's top-ranked offense.

But then the formula that led them to most of their early-season victories changed before their longest stretch of games at home.

The ingredients changing meant the recipe for success also had to be altered – which the Lakers successfully pulled off during the 3–1 homestand that ended with Monday's victory over the Jazz.

Doncic cooled off from his sizzling start to the season during the homestand, averaging 29.5 points (38.5% shooting, 23.5% on 3-pointers), after averaging 39 points (48.6% shooting, 40.6% on 3s) beforehand.

Utah Jazz forward Kyle Filipowski (2) goes up for a basket as Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler (14) defends. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong

Reaves wasn't available, missing the last five games because of a bruised left heel. The Lakers are hopeful he'll return during Friday's road game against the Spurs.

Which led to the Lakers leaning on their defense to pull out most of their recent wins.

"We have a standard and we have to play to that standard and do what we're supposed to," Collin Sexton said. "When you're playing to a standard, it doesn't matter who's in and who's out. We all have to help. It doesn't matter who's coming into the game, we all have a role to play to do what the person in front of us did."

The Lakers held the Hornets to 114 points in their overtime win Nov. 17, allowed 109 points in the Nov. 18 loss to the Jazz, held the Kings to 104 points in Friday's win before holding the Jazz to 94 points on Monday, which is the fewest amount of points a team has scored against the Lakers this season.

Los Angeles Lakers forward Jarred Vanderbilt (2) vies for the ball against Utah Jazz forward Kyle Filipowski. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong

Their halfcourt defense has been a strength of the Lakers throughout the season.

But they cleaned up some of their transition defensive concerns. They remained disruptive, recording at least 16 turnovers in each game of the homestand. And using more zone defense, sometimes with full-court pressure, gave the Lakers a boost on that end of the floor.

"We have a lot of like disruptors defensively," Jake LaRavia said. "We do a good job at just creating pressure for the other team, whether it's deflections or just ball pressure, and kind of making them uncomfortable in bringing the ball up the court. It's obviously been working for us, so we're going to keep doing it 'til it stops working."

The Lakers' defensive rating improved from No. 17 to No. 10 during the homestand – albeit against inferior opponents that have a combined record of 9–43.

They're going to need Reaves available and improved play from Doncic as the level of competition picks up with the four-game trip post-Thanksgiving that features matchups against the Spurs, Grizzlies and Rockets. Those are three of the four teams closest to the Lakers in the top of the Western Conference standings.

But even though it wasn't always pretty, the Lakers showed they can at least win in other ways outside of what they showed in the first few weeks of the season.

"Austin is a very, very important piece to this team, and so seeing how we compete without him, not at our full strength, that's good," Kessler said. "It builds resiliency. Because [you're] not going to be always [at] your full strength. Things happen, it's a long season, so it's encouraging to see."

#2584. Jermod McCoy shows promise during 1st start for Las Vegas Raiders in Week 11 vs. Denver Broncos

The Las Vegas Raiders have been searching for answers at cornerback throughout the season, often deploying a three-man rotation between Darien Porter, Hezekiah Masses and Jermod McCoy at one of the two starting spots on the perimeter this season. However, in Week 11 against the Denver Broncos, the coaching staff decided to let McCoy take all of the reps, for better or worse.

According to Pro Football Focus, the numbers on the fourth-round pick's first start were a mixed bag. He was targeted five times and gave up two catches (one drop) for 55 yards while recording a pass breakup. So it was far from a perfect outing, but the Tennessee product showed promise on tape where the stats leave out some context. With that in mind, let's dive into the film.

Let's get the negative reps out of the way to end on a high note. And while the result here is bad, this is far from a terrible rep.

The problem is that when the Broncos motion the slot receiver across the formation to get into a three-by-one set, the Raiders respond by getting into a single-high coverage that leaves McCoy one-on-one with Jaylen Waddle, who has a reputation as one of the best deep threats in the NFL.

Still, the rookie corner does a decent job of staying patient at the line of scrimmage by not completely opening his hips until Waddle commits to the outside release. Then, McCoy uses his inside hand to help slow the receiver down a bit and run with the receiver stride for stride, meaning this is perfect coverage against a go route. However, it isn't, and the problems begin at about the 50-yard line.

That's where Waddle starts to tip his route by picking his shoulders and head up to hit the breaks on the curl route. But McCoy doesn't, or is late to see that, and ends up running right by his man, giving up plenty of separation for a 19-yard catch.

To cut the fourth-round pick some slack, especially with no safety help over the top, this is a tough assignment with Waddle's speed. However, he can still use this rep to build confidence, knowing that he was able to run with Waddle. This can be a learning moment for McCoy, recognizing that he can trust his speed and look for the route indicators that receivers give him moving forward.

This is a similar rep, just against Troy Franklin, who can also fly with a 4.41-second 40-yard dash time at the 2024 NFL Combine.

Again, McCoy shows decent patience at the line of scrimmage to avoid opening up the gate and getting burnt. But he does get turned around a bit with Franklin using an outside jab step to set up his inside release. Still, McCoy isn't out of position initially by using his hands to help stay in phase. The issue is he holds on too long, which slows him down and leads to the receiver breaking free later in the route.

Luckily, the wideout had one of the more comical drops of the season, with the ball doinking off his helmet for an incompletion. So, the corner gets away with this one. Also, it looks like he was supposed to have some sort of help over the top.

The Raiders are running a unique coverage here, where the outside corners (McCoy and Eric Stokes at the bottom of the screen) are playing man while the four other defensive backs (Hezekiah Masses, Treydan Stukes, Jeremy Chinn and Taron Johnson) are executing a pattern match zone coverage.

Notice how both Johnson and Chinn converge on the receiver in the middle of the field despite the pass going over the top of the defense. It's impossible to know for certain without having the exact play call and coverage rules, but I'd imagine one of those two is supposed to help against the deep route.

This is a rep that goes down as a negative one on the ledger since the Broncos get an explosive play out of it, but it isn't nearly as bad as the scorebook shows for McCoy.

Not only does Denver run a flea flicker, but they also have the outside receiver (Marvin Mims, who runs a 4.38-second 40-yard dash) motion across the formation for a wheel route while executing a switch release with the receiver at the top of the screen. But the rookie isn't fooled, staying at his landmark in the Cover 4 call and passing off the outside receiver to pick up the wheel route.

McCoy is in a good spot to defend the route, squeezing the receiver toward the sideline and staying in the receiver's hip pocket throughout the rep. However, he starts to stumble around the 12-yard line and trips right before the ball arrives, while Chinn can't get there in time to help, resulting in the big gain that set up a Broncos touchdown.

What's most encouraging about this play is that in previous games, McCoy had a lot of issues against these types of concepts in zone coverage. In his limited playing time prior to this past Sunday, he often looked confused or like he was thinking too much and unsure who to cover when playing zone, especially against route combinations where he had to pick up and pass off receivers.

So, despite this being a big gain, the rookie is showing growth here. He just needs to be better at staying on his feet to finish the play.

Moving onto the positive reps, while the incompletion here is a result of Bo Nix making the wrong read and Courtland Sutton running into Johnson, it's still solid coverage from McCoy.

Denver dials up a mesh concept, where Sutton is working across the field on a deep drag or over route to set a pick for the slot receiver (No. 13 Pat Bryant). That's a good play call by Sean Payton because it catches Las Vegas in man coverage and Bryant is open, which is where Nix should go with the ball.

But from McCoy's perspective, he's in a perfect position to defend the over route, avoiding any contact on the pick and running stride-for-stride with Sutton. In fact, the corner might get an interception if the receiver's route doesn't get cut short. It's the difference between his eyes being on his man (which is where they should be in man coverage) and on the quarterback, making it more difficult to adjust to the ball in the air.

As a side note, Klint Kubiak went viral for saying at halftime that the referees needed to call the game both ways. Kubiak has a good point with this play because if Cody White was called for offensive pass interference in the end zone — a penalty that wiped away a touchdown — then Sutton should get flagged here, too.

Here, we'll get another rep from McCoy in press coverage against Franklin on a go route. This time, he does an ever better job of staying patient at the line of scrimmage against the inside jab step from Franklin to avoid opening the gate too early.

Once the receiver commits to the outside release, then the corner opens his hips to turn and run. He manages to stay in the receiver's hip pocket throughout the route while widening the wideout toward the sideline to give the quarterback less room to complete the pass. So, Nix tries to throw back shoulder, but McCoy recognizes that Franklin is slowing down and throttles with his man to contest the catch for an incompletion.

That's perfect coverage against a go route, taking away the deep shot and the back shoulder throw. The problem is that Johnson gets flagged for illegal contact against Waddle, making McCoy's rep go all for naught.

I saved the best play McCoy made for last so that we can end on the highest of high notes. Ironically, this is the first target that came his way during the game.

Part of what's so impressive is that Rob Leonard calls the rookie's number, leaving him one-on-one against Waddle, the Broncos' best receiver. Denver even gets a coverage indicator pre-snap, motioning a receiver from across the formation, which Masses follows to tip that Vegas is in man.

A lot of coordinators would have the secondary rotate, where McCoy widens with the motion to stay on the outside receiver and avoid showing the defense's hand. But Leonard shows faith in the fourth-round pick, and the latter proves why his coach had confidence in him.

Again, McCoy does a good job of staying patient on the line of scrimmage while playing press, not opening the gate until Waddle commits to the outside release. Also, he uses his hands well to help stay in phase throughout the rep, running stride-for-stride with the receiver against the slot fade route. Nix still tries to drop it in the bucket, and McCoy recognizes that Waddle is looking up for the ball, turning his head to locate it in the air too. That allows him to come up with a PBU and keep the Broncos out of the end zone on third down.

While the fourth-rounder still has plenty to prove over the next couple of months, he showed why he was considered a draft steal and the most talented corner on the roster in Denver. That should keep McCoy in the starting lineup for the foreseeable future, especially since the defense has spent the entire season searching for cornerback help.

We're onto Week 6! Here is the 9-cat version of my risers and fallers list. These rankings are for rest-of-season 9-cat leagues, and I'm leaning on Yahoo's rankings from the last two weeks and last month. Efficiency matters more here than in points leagues, and it's the main thing separating these six players. Let's get into it!

Ausar is averaging 10.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 5.4 assists, 1.6 steals and 1 block on 55% shooting through 16 games, and he's been even better lately. He's eighth over the last two weeks and 30th over the last month. He leads the Pistons in rebounding and had a 17-board game against Philadelphia on Nov. 4. The weak spots are well known. Those with punt-3 builds get the most out of him, since he positively adds value in rebounds, assists, stocks and field goal percentage. The jump to 73% from the line is another win, as he doesn't hurt you nearly as badly as he used to.

I have him 57th, as I anticipate Jalen Duren's return will impact his numbers to some degree. Either way, he's exceeding expectations in what could be a breakout campaign.

Smith is averaging 14.1 points, 7.5 rebounds, 2.1 3s and 1 block in 25.3 minutes, shooting 55% from the field with 0.9 turnovers per game. That mix of 3s, blocks, field goal percentage and low turnovers is why he grades out well in 9-cat without much volume. He's 14th over the last two weeks and 26th over the last month. He was drafted in just 8% of Yahoo leagues, so if you scooped him up off waivers, you're playing with house money.

I'm moving him up to 65th, from 99th, but not higher because much of this production came with Nic Claxton sidelined. Caleb Wilson is also out, and Claxton is still ramping up, so Smith's role should hold for now. I could be too low on him. Continue to hold.

McDaniels is 11th over the last two weeks and 18th over the last month.  The bump in usage comes from Anthony Edwards' absence. Edwards is out until late January after knee surgery, and McDaniels has absorbed a bigger share of the offense without losing efficiency. He's averaging 18.4 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.2 steals, 0.9 blocks and 1.6 3s in 33.9 minutes, shooting 56% from the field and 85% from the line.

He's positive in eight of nine categories, with turnovers (2.2 per game) the only negative. I don't value turnovers that much, especially when he's so productive across other areas of fantasy. Some of that scoring should come back down when Edwards returns, which is why I have him 30th, up from 43rd. I wouldn't sell, even though his play is on another level right now.

Hart is 233rd over the last two weeks and 176th over the last month. His scoring is down to 6.6 points per game from 12.0 last season, and he's shooting 34% from the field and 60% from the line. He's still contributing 6.7 rebounds and 4.0 assists, which keeps him rosterable, but his steals have dipped recently and he's listed as questionable with a right shoulder sprain. In 9-cat, the low percentages make it a bigger problem. The good news is that his minutes appear to be trending back up. Landry Shamet's been eating into his minutes because of his shooting, but over the past two games, Hart's averaging 37 minutes per gam. He's also coming off a 10-11-10 triple-double, which could be a nice selling point if you're concerned about his ROS outlook.

I have him 120th, down from 72nd. I'd hold in 12-team 9-cat leagues for now since his shooting should improve, but he's not as bad as Mikal Bridges, who was near drop status.

Gobert is 239th over the last two weeks and 289th over the last month. His rebound and block rates are both down: he's averaging 10.6 rebounds and 1.0 block in 29.2 minutes, compared to 11.5 and 1.6 last season. He's also shooting 46% from the line on 4.7 attempts per game. That's way too much volume for someone shooting so poorly.

Reid has the volume in his first season in Charlotte: 17.7 points, 8.3 rebounds and 2.5 3s in 31.5 minutes. The problem is efficiency. #2580. Aaron Rodgers just left Mike McCarthy, Steelers in untenable situation

If Aaron Rodgers had only accused Mike McCarthy of falling behind on film study and game preparation, perhaps McCarthy could have explained himself.

If the disgruntled Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback had only accused his head coach of breaking down the team with "1-2-3 Packers" rather than "1-2-3 Steelers," perhaps McCarthy could have laughed off the slip as a joke.

If Rodgers had only alleged that his play-caller fell asleep and snored in meetings or only alleged that his head coach said he did not need to ingratiate himself to defensive players or only alleged that McCarthy had missed walkthroughs, a franchise currently still on pace to make the playoffs could chart its next step more clearly.

Instead, as Rodgers scorched McCarthy with reckless abandon Wednesday on the "Pat McAfee Show," the four-time MVP left his coach — seemingly intentionally — with an untenable situation.

Aaron Rodgers' working relationship with head coach Mike McCarthy blew up spectacularly in the past 48 hours.

McCarthy is not in his second decade with the Green Bay Packers basking in the aftermath of the Lombardi glow as he once did when his tension with Rodgers boiled into the spotlight.

He's not several years into a Dallas tenure that featured three straight 12-win seasons as he was when Cowboys team owner and general manager Jerry Jones and McCarthy's disagreement over pay led to a lame-duck contract year and ultimate nonrenewal.

McCarthy doesn't even have a proven quarterback to call plays for the rest of the season, which by the way is coming fast as the Steelers host the Denver Broncos on Black Friday.

Stay quiet, and the Steelers know the NFL world — and likely beyond, as Rodgers' platform tends to stretch – will believe that Rodgers' allegations are at least partially true and McCarthy has lost his team. Multiple Steelers reporters emerging from open locker room Wednesday with sourced corroborations of Rodgers' account does not help McCarthy's case chalking this up to the latest Rodgers conspiracy.

Speak, and McCarthy faces overanalysis of any comments – not only from outside the building but mostly importantly from within. He's spent less than a year coaching his hometown team. This roster is not primarily rooted in young, impressionable players who have no comparison point for the work ethic and culture expected of an NFL head coach. Instead, players like 16th-year defensive lineman Cam Heyward and 10th-year outside linebacker T.J. Watt and 11th-year safety Jalen Ramsey all remember the culture longtime Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin established even as his ability to win in the postseason waned.

Adding to McCarthy's challenges: Rodgers built relationships with this locker room for an entire season before McCarthy arrived. It's Rodgers who fought with Heyward and Watt and tight end Pat Freiermuth to advance to the playoffs last season, and Rodgers for whom receiver Ben Skowronek bought a birthday cake nearly a year ago. It's Rodgers whom receiver DK Metcalf shared a bathroom with across two training-camp stints in Latrobe, Pennsylvania, and Rodgers who mentored the younger quarterbacks in the room even when McCarthy arrived.

"If we were a married couple in Green Bay, now we're an old married couple," McCarthy told Yahoo Sports in training camp when discussing Rodgers' presence in offensive meetings. "He talks a lot more now. I always thought I was a good listener, but I think I do more listening now. And actually it's really refreshing because to sit there and listen to him talk about footwork and just all the different things. And it's really good for the younger players. And I think Mason appreciates it, too."

McCarthy elaborated on Rodgers guiding veteran Mason Rudolph, 2025 sixth-round draft pick Will Howard and 2026 third-round pick Drew Allar.

"He is very forthcoming, particularly with Will and Drew, more Drew, just because Drew wasn't there last year. Will and Aaron have a very strong relationship. And obviously Aaron and Mason have a strong personal relationship, too. But yeah, I mean, footwork, reads, just particulars on a lot of plays."

It's Rodgers to whom the team was listening during training camp meetings – and Rodgers to whom the locker room was reportedly listening Wednesday from the locker room as the team's nearly-former quarterback aired his grievances on McAfee. The Steelers releasing Rodgers does not erase the impact of his words.

Rodgers' decades of complaints don't change McCarthy's résumé: He's won 60.7% of games across 19 seasons (180-116-2), advancing 12 times to the postseason and winning 11 games including a Super Bowl. Even this season, the Steelers have a winning record and would advance to the playoffs if the regular season ended today.

But it's unrealistic to think McCarthy's credibility and reputation won't change after players listen to Rodgers publicize his allegations — some of which players are now telling reporters they have witnessed themselves.

Sure, Rodgers dabbled during his McAfee appearance in lines like "the only difference between conspiracy and the truth is time." The quarterback admitted that he wanted to call his own plays and demanded McCarthy at least give up play-calling, telling McCarthy to release him if he would not. The backdrop of all of this, of course, is a 42-year-old quarterback in the final year of his Hall of Fame career getting benched after leading the team to a winning record.

But as Rodgers' interview stretched on, and as he kept talking through McAfee's seeming attempts to wrap the segment, a truth became clear: No matter what percentage of Rodgers' allegations were true, and no matter how much of an axe viewers knew he had to grind, Rodgers' 30+-minute segment railing against his longtime colleague who remains the head coach of an NFL team will not be ignored.

McCarthy, along with coaches and players across the Steelers organization, find themselves in an untenable situation.

And hey, the Broncos will arrive in less than 48 hours with postseason hopes on the line.

#2579. Los Angeles court approves two restraining orders for LeBron James' family due to trespassing incidents

While LeBron James is in Philadelphia (well, living in New York and helicoptering into Philadelphia) to play with the 76ers, his family has stayed in Los Angeles — and has been dealing with trespassers.

One man was arrested, and another showed up at the James family home in the Los Angeles area — in a gated community with security — and claimed the property was his. Now, a California court has approved two temporary restraining orders on behalf of LeBron James' family, one for each man, according to court documents reviewed by The Athletic.

One of the filings, submitted by James' wife, Savannah, said that on Nov. 6, Jaliere Zacchaeus McWhite, a 22-year-old man from Florida, evaded private community security and the family's own security, climbing onto an adjacent property to cross onto the James' property. McWhite then entered the residence through the front door, moments after members of the James family left the door unlocked after exiting the home. Los Angeles police arrived at the scene and arrested McWhite for trespassing and burglary-related offenses, the filing said...

A second temporary restraining order against William Norman Rahman, a 55-year-old man from Texas, describes Rahman having mail and packages delivered to the family's home dating back to December 2025. In October, the filing said, security observed Rahman loitering near the property with luggage. He returned to the property's driveway, again with luggage, on Nov. 14, and, according to the filing, told police that the home belonged to him.

The court documents say all of this has been disturbing to the family and their sense of security. LeBron's wife, Savannah, and 12-year-old daughter, Zhuri, both live in the home. Stalking of high-profile athletes, or attempts to burglarize their home when they are away, have become increasingly common in recent years.

#2578. Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to New Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He said at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1

For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

Goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

In the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+

Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

That said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B

#2575. Christian Gonzalez's blunt response to Patriots' defensive struggles

New England Patriots star cornerback Christian Gonzalez recognizes that the team's defense has fallen short of expectations in recent weeks.

Speaking to reporters before practice on Tuesday, Gonzalez detailed his view of the defense's play of late, but ended on an optimistic note about how the team should move forward after its slump, per WEEI.

"Obviously, we don't like what we've put out there the past two weeks," Gonzalez said. "But at the same time — You don't look back on nothing. ...You learn from what you've got beat on, but you don't ever look back and be like, 'Ahh, this is bad. This is still disappointing.' We're professional athletes, we're grown men, we know what we put out there ain't right. But you move on and be ready for this one."

The Patriots have struggled to contain opposing offenses, as they surrendered 30 points to the Chicago Bears, 45 points to the Green Bay Packers, and 35 points to the Detroit Lions. Those performances have highlighted ongoing defensive concerns and raised questions about the unit's ability to consistently stop high-caliber offenses.

New England is in search of answers coming out of their bye week. Better execution in all three phases of the field along the defensive front will be essential. The Patriots also need to generate more pressure on opposing quarterbacks while limiting big plays and sharpening up their coverage in critical situations. With the season entering a critical stretch, all of those key areas will be necessary for the defense to deliver on if New England hopes to remain competitive in the playoff race.

Looking ahead, the road will not get any easier for the Patriots. New England will face the struggling Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12 before a tough three-game stretch against the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings and Kansas City Chiefs.

Gonzalez and his teammates will be tasked with rejuvenating their defensive identity and establishing greater consistency for a possible late run.

#2573. Sean McVay on Puka Nacua: 'Can't say for certain' what his Rams future will be amid pending free agency

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is likely out for the remainder of the season after undergoing surgery for an MCL injury he sustained on the final offensive snap of the team's Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders. Nacua is also set to be a free agent this coming offseason now that his rookie deal is set to expire, and Rams head coach Sean McVay delivered a mixed message about Nacua's future with the team.

"Yeah, we have a lot of guys that are free agents," McVay told reporters earlier this week. "What I've tried to really do is focus on right here, right now. He's obviously a guy that is a very important piece for us for now and for the future, but there are a lot of guys that fall under that category."

That makes it sound like Nacua will be back with the Rams, and there's not much to speculate about. But a later quote indicated there may not be as much certainty on that front, mostly because McVay said those words pretty much exactly.

"I can't say for certain anything," McVay said. "Here's what I'm not interested in: something being taken out of context because my focus and concentration are on a Friday practice, even though I know it's Monday. I am trying to see how well we can play as a team against an excellent opponent [the Green Bay Packers] on Wednesday night.

"When you go through the amount of free agents that we have, Puka is a huge part of the conversation that you love, but there are also guys that are part of his draft class. There are guys on our offensive line, there are some guys defensively — so there are a lot of guys that are up that, as of right now, would not be under contract. There are mechanics that we'd like to be able to try to figure out how to keep these really good players and people that we love, and certainly Puka is at the forefront of our mind."

In addition to Nacua, the Rams have Kevin Dotson, Coleman Shelton, Steve Avila, Byron Young, Josh Wallace, Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Davante Adams, Omar Speights and Kobie Turner, among others, set to hit free agency this offseason. While the Rams' $75.2 million in projected cap space is the fifth-most in the league (according to Over the Cap), that's a lot of players. Many of the Rams' pending free agents are significant contributors. However, none of them is nearly as integral to the team's success as Nacua is.

Nacua is the Rams' best offensive player. He is one of the best receivers in the league, and he's well on his way to being one of the best in recent memory if he can stay healthy. His 383 catches are the seventh-most all time through four seasons despite the fact that he's only played 3.5 years so far. His 4,906 receiving yards are the seventh-most as well. He's the all-time leader in receiving yards per game (96.2), and he's averged over 100 yards per game in each of the last two seasons.

But he's also somewhat unreliable from a health perspective, as a regular visitor to the medical tent and someone who will have missed 17 of the team's 51 games over the last three seasons by the time this year is up. And he's had very public off-field issues over the last year or so that resulted in a three-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy. The league reportedly did not know Nacua needed season-ending surgery when it suspended him and allowed him to serve the suspension during his stint on injured reserve.

It wouldn't be surprising, then, if the Rams were at least somewhat hesitant to commit what it would take to secure a long-term contract. The best wide receivers in the league are making over $40 million per year. Jaxson Smith-Njigba averages $42.5 million per year on his extension. To lock Nacua in, it would likely take a deal that exceeds JSN's average annual value, given Nacua's track record.

Meanwhile, the franchise tag is projected to be worth "only" $30.91 million next season, according to Over the Cap, so that may be an option for the Rams to explore instead. That would allow them to retain Nacua for at least next season, even if they don't reach a long-term agreement, while also letting them negotiate an extension and retain the ability to explore potential trade opportunities if they decide they don't want to commit to him long term. And it seems like him not being around long-term is at least a possibility in the ether.

"Very uncertain, up in the air as it pertains to the future with the L.A. Rams because going into free agency he's got two different injuries, including a significant MCL injury that Sean McVay says will keep him out a few months," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler said this weekend. "Probably ends his tenure with the Rams — plus the three-game suspension for the off-field stuff this offseason, so it's just not the kind of way you want to go into free agency with momentum. On the field, he's the best free agent in 2027 of any player, so the Rams have got to sort that out."

Fowler may have misspoken when he said the injury probably ends Nacua's tenure with the Rams. Based on the rest of the quote, it seems like he meant that the injury will end Nacua's season with the Rams. But the idea that his future is uncertain at all is obviously notable, given how important he is to the team. If Nacua isn't going to be on the team, then the Rams don't have much to build their offense around in the future, whenever the post-Matthew Stafford era begins. They wouldn't exactly be setting Ty Simpson up for success if they decided to go that route.

Because Nacua is so good and so important to the Rams' offensive infrastructure, it seems likely they'll eventually come to an agreement on an extension. But the lack of certainty in that regard, both from McVay and in outside reporting, makes this situation one to watch.

#2571. Aaron Rodgers rips Mike McCarthy, says coach fell asleep in meeting and mistakenly called team 'Packers'; league sources reportedly corroborate quarterback's account

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers did not stay silent for long following his surprise benching. And shortly after Rodgers publicly accused Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy of everything from sleeping in meetings to mistakenly calling the team the "Packers," the franchise reportedly decided to release the veteran quarterback.

Rodgers, a four-time NFL MVP, joined the "Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday afternoon to address his benching … and he did not hold back when it came to sharing his side of how the events of the week unfolded — or when it comes to his feelings about McCarthy.

"I found out that I was gonna be inactive on a phone call last night from Pat Freiermuth," Rodgers said in the interview. "I was talking to Muth and a couple of the guys, and he said, 'I can't believe they're doing this.' And I said, 'Doing what?' I didn't know. And he told me, and obviously, there had been a lot of things in motion at that point. I didn't hear from Mike [McCarthy]."

"Mike and I talked for a long time the last few days, and that word [benching] never came up," Rodgers continued.

After that, Rodgers released a windfall of scathing accusations against McCarthy, ripping into his head coach for a series of events over the past week that "ultimately led to where we're at now."

Rodgers said McCarthy arrived late to a quarterbacks meeting last Wednesday, in which the coach fell asleep and was snoring. Rodgers accused McCarthy of missing an offensive meeting the following day and also missed the Friday walkthrough.

"Doesn't come to the first walkthrough," Rodgers said. "Doesn't come to the protection walkthrough on Thursday. Saturday, he misses the morning meeting, and we don't have a team meeting Saturday night for whatever reason in Philly. And then comes Sunday, when obviously we struggled, and the product wasn't great."

Rodgers also ripped into McCarthy's relationships with players on the team, alleging that he didn't care to get to know the defense and had lost many of those players well before the end.

"There were some guys early on that were … didn't like the way things were going, especially defensive guys. Mike didn't want to get to know the defense," Rodgers said. "At one point, I told him, 'You should really lean into the defensive guys a little bit more and talk to those guys,' and he said, 'Well, I don't think I need to.' And I said, 'Well, I disagree with that.'"

"He already kind of lost a lot of those guys, and I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was, at halftime, toward the end of it … he says, 'Alright, 1-2-3-Packers!' That's what he broke it down on in the locker room," Rodgers said. "We all looked around, going, 'What the f***? What is going on? Where's his head at, at this point?"

The Steelers went on to lose that game, 19-16, snapping a seven-game losing streak for the Philadelphia Eagles. Rodgers took five sacks in the loss, completing 30-of-44 pass attempts for 227 yards and a score.

Clearly, the loss was a tipping point for Rodgers.

"I went in on Monday, and I just said, "Hey, this last week, this is not what we talked about. We've had these conversations for months now. And it began as a concerned friend about somebody who's unhealthy. If you're sleeping in meetings, you're unhealthy. If you're not coming to everything you should be coming to as a playcaller, [you're unhealthy].

"I mean, how many quarterbacks around the league are dealing with the same type of stuff? I gave you one week. I could go week-by-week throughout the season on stuff that was going on.

"Monday, we're having this conversation, and I said, 'We need to make a change for the betterment of the team.'"

The change Rodgers was hoping for was a change in playcaller. But instead, the team made a change at quarterback.

How do Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers move forward after this?

Well … apparently, they don't. Rodgers acknowledged as much nearing the end of his McAfee appearance, saying the "ship has sailed" on a return to the team.

Soon after Rodgers' interview concluded, it was reported that the Steelers were releasing Rodgers, according to Pittsburgh Post-Gazette beat writer Gerry Dulac. Other reports have since confirmed the same.

The real question now is how the Steelers will move forward with McCarthy, after multiple league sources have corroborated Rodgers' account to ESPN.

#2569. Ranking NFL division races from first to worst: NFC North, NFC South entertaining for very different reasons

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The NFC East might be the best example of the NFL's unpredictable nature. Earlier this season, it made history by becoming the first division to go winless over a two-week span in which every team played both weeks. Yes, that included the infamous Commanders-Giants tie that featured a fumble and an all-time clock mismanagement on the final two drives.

Then in Week 11, the division went 4-0 collectively, with the Eagles, Giants, and Commanders all springing upsets over AFC teams currently in the playoff field. A $10 NFC East parlay of the Eagles beating the Steelers, the Giants beating the Jaguars, the Commanders beating the Bengals and the Cowboys beating the Titans would have netted you a handsome $345.51.

As Al Pacino, playing Michael Corleone in The Godfather Part III, said: "Just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in!"

Ahead of a packed Thanksgiving week chock full of divisional matchups, we rank all eight division races, taking into account the quality of the teams involved, the quality of the races themselves and the potential for pandemonium.

The NFC North's main quest is potentially being the first team to place all four teams in the postseason. But the division race itself is a thriller, especially with Lions-Bears looming on Thanksgiving. Yes, Detroit looks like the clear NFC North favorite for now, but a Chicago win on Turkey Day would boost the Bears' chance to win the division to 45%. Regardless, this race projects to end in a thriller: In Week 18, the Lions play the Packers, and the Bears play the Vikings.

Does it get much better than a 50/50 split? Technically, our projections give Denver a 50.1% chance and Kansas City a 49.9% chance, if you're into that level of detail. The two teams have already played both of their head-to-head matchups (they split). The Broncos do have, on paper, an easier schedule remaining, which certainly helps.

All of a sudden, this division race doesn't look fun-bad and might just be ... fun! The Giants and Cowboys have the eighth- and ninth-hardest remaining schedules, while the Commanders don't face a team with a winning record until Week 16. A finishing stretch featuring Giants at Cowboys in Week 17 followed by Cowboys at Commanders and Eagles at Giants in Week 18 could provide plenty of twists and turns.

Last year, the Buccaneers beat the Panthers in Week 18 to stay alive, only to lose the NFC South on a tiebreaker the next day when the Falcons beat the Saints. Could we see similar madness this year? Week 12 will go a long way: If Tampa Bay beats Carolina on Monday Night Football, its chance to win the division jumps to 53%, per our calculations.

The NFC South: It might be bad, but it's certainly not boring!

Even with the bunched standings at the top, our projections see Cincinnati as a clear favorite. The Bengals have several games where they should be huge favorites: Saints, at Panthers, at Colts, Ravens. It's far from wrapped up, though, and two games vs. the Browns loom large.

The 49ers look like the best team in the NFL, and with a three-game lead in the division, this one might not have much drama. If that changes, it must start this week, when the Seahawks visit San Francisco. A Seattle win would only knock the 49ers' NFC West title chances to 81%, but it'd be a start.

Never say never, but it's hard to see this one getting competitive, even after the Texans won and the Jaguars lost in Week 11. Houston needs another upset loss or two by Jacksonville. If that happens, remember Houston holds the head-to-head tiebreaker. That could turn up the heat.

With Drake Maye out until the final week or two at best, it would take something catastrophic (basically a Josh Allen injury) for this to be an actual race. And then, Tommy DeVito trying to chase down Kyle Allen would be more sad than fun.

#2566. NFL news, live updates: Steelers reportedly release Aaron Rodgers after he delivers rant on Mike McCarthy; 49ers QB Brock Purdy dealing with ankle injury

Week 12 of the NFL season kicks off with a rare Wednesday matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, prepping us for a full Thanksgiving feast of football the following day, headlined by an MVP showcase between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday night.

Ahead of that matchup, the Steelers made headlines by reportedly benching veteran quarterback and former MVP Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph for Week 12 after recent struggles on offense.

This storyline then reached a fever pitch on Wednesday when Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" and went scorched-earth on a rant about head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers accused McCarthy of repeatedly falling asleep in meetings and ending a team breakdown with "1-2-3 Let's go Packers."

Shortly after his appearance on the show, the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac reported that Rodgers was being released. The quarterback had said on the show that he was "not going back to Pittsburgh."

We're watching plenty of injuries ahead of the action, including Las Vegas Raiders All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers, who missed Week 11 with an ankle injury, though he was reportedly pushing to play in that matchup. The Kansas City Chiefs have already ruled out running back Kenneth Walker III for his third consecutive game with a groin injury, giving rookie Emmett Johnson the nod for a Thanksgiving contest with the Buffalo Bills.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 11.

San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is dealing with an ankle injury, head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Wednesday.

Shanahan specified that Purdy does not have a high-ankle injury, but the quarterback may not be able to play Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks.

If Purdy can't start the NFC West divisional game, backup quarterback Mac Jones is expected to take over.

San Francisco is 9-1 and leads both the division and the NFC. The 49ers had their bye week in Week 8 and have won three consecutive games.

Purdy is having one of the best seasons of his career. In just 10 games, he has already thrown more touchdowns (23) than in each of his last two seasons (20). Purdy has thrown for 2,624 yards and five interceptions, and has added 222 additional yards and two more scores on the ground.

While the Rams continue taking injury hits on offense, they are getting a reinforcement on defense.

Defensive end Kobie Turner has been activated ahead of Wednesday night's game against the Packers.

Turner had been on IR because of a groin injury and last played on October 18. He heads into tonight's game with just seven sacks on the year.

The Steelers have reportedly released veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers, per Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac.

Rodgers' release was reportedly expedited after the quarterback went scorched-earth on former head coach Mike McCarthy on Wednesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show."

The NFL went out of its way to schedule five compelling matchups for Thanksgiving Eve, Thanksgiving and Black Friday.

The schedule comes out in May, and things can change dramatically over six months. Yet four of the five matchups have held up very well. That's not a bad percentage, even if the Eagles and Cowboys have let us down. Everyone will watch those two marquee franchises anyway.

There's a lot on the line in terms of the playoff race during this week. We rank the most important games, in terms of what's at stake.

Veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has signed with the Washington Commanders practice squad as a free agent, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday.

Aiyuk was released by the 49ers on Monday and passed through waivers on Tuesday, going unclaimed. Now, he reunites with his former teammate at Arizona State, quarterback Jayden Daniels.

The Commanders, fresh off a stunning upset over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 11, have been in need of help at receiver following a season-ending injury to star wideout Terry McLaurin. The team sits at 4-5-1, just two games back from the New York Giants, who hold the lead in the NFC East.

This marks a fresh start for the 28-year-old, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract extension with the 49ers ahead of the 2024 season but played just seven games on the new deal. He tore his ACL and MCL on Oct. 20, 2024, ending his season.

The Chiefs are looking at another game without star running back Kenneth Walker III. Despite returning to practice Tuesday, Walker will reportedly not play against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving, according to multiple reports.

It will mark the third straight game Walker will miss due to the issue.

Prior to the injury, Walker was well on his way toward posting his finest season in the NFL. Through eight games, the running back already rushed for 872 yards and seven touchdowns. He also hauled in 26 catches for 172 yards and four receiving scores.

There were four MVPs, 10 Pro Bowls, a Super Bowl championship, dozens of highlights that defied belief over 22 seasons, and it all seems to end with a quick statement from the team after most of Pittsburgh had already gone to sleep.

It's not like Rodgers has played great this season, which he said will be his last in the NFL. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy was asked this week if Rodgers was still the team's starter, so it wasn't completely out of the blue that he got benched.

It was still abrupt, and with some unusual timing. There was no time to celebrate the end of a legendary career or even realize that the snaps he took Sunday might be his last.

It's just done, barring some other turn of events over the final few weeks of the season.

The Steelers made the decision late Tuesday night to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers. On Wednesday morning, the team began dealing with the fallout from that decision.

Rodgers was reportedly not in the building early Wednesday when the Steelers held their morning team meeting at 8 a.m. ET, per ESPN's Brooke Pryor.

Additional reporting suggested Rodgers was excused from going to team facilities the day after it was announced he was benched.

At that meeting, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy officially announced the quarterback change to the rest of the team. That decision was reportedly "not a popular" one within the locker room, per The Athletic.

While Rodgers struggled this season, he was still well-liked by his teammates, per Pryor.

The Pittsburgh Steelers announced Tuesday night that Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback on Friday against the Denver Broncos.

The Eagles listed star running back Saquon Barkley as a full practice participant on Tuesday.

The injury report did note that it was just a walkthrough, but yesterday, when Philly did not practice, the team listed Barkley as a limited practice participant due to a neck injury as well as an illness.

The Eagles play the Cowboys on Thursday afternoon for Thanksgiving.

Brandon Aiyuk may have a new home sooner than later.

The former 49ers receiver is scheduled to visit with the Washington Commanders. That's according to his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, who told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Aiyuk will meet with the Commanders on Wednesday.

Ayiuk cleared waivers on Tuesday after previously being released by the 49ers, concluding a protracted and contentious breakup with the franchise.

After finally being released by the San Francisco 49ers, veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has cleared waivers, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter, who also reported Tuesday that Aiyuk would like to sign with a new team soon.

He's expected to attract interest from a few teams, including the Washington Commanders, per Schefter.

The Niners releasing Aiyuk marked the end of a months-long standoff between the team and player. Aiyuk missed the entire 2025 NFL season after recovering from a knee injury he suffered in 2024, just months after signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the team. He suffered a torn ACL and MCL in late October 2024 and hasn't played a snap in the league since.

San Francisco had a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk. It expired on Monday, and as a result, the franchise opted to release Aiyuk, giving both the team and the wide receiver a fresh start.

Denver Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins has been suspended for one game for conduct detrimental to the team, according to head coach Sean Payton.

Payton did not get into specifics and told reporters he would not comment further on the situation.

Dobbins, 27, is in his second season with the Broncos. He has rushed for 324 yards and 3 touchdowns on 99 carries, adding 31 receiving yards on 9 catches. Last year, Dobbins compiled 772 rushing yards and 4 TDs.

The suspension leaves Denver will be without its leading rusher for Friday's Week 12 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Jonah Coleman (302 rushing yards in 6 games) will presumably take over as the starter.

Micah Parsons is officially activated off the Physically Unable to Perform list, Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst announced on Tuesday.

So the All-Pro pass rusher appears to be ready to play in Wednesday's Thanksgiving Eve matchup versus the Los Angeles Rams. Parsons had been listed as questionable for the game.

Parsons has been sidelined while recovering from a torn ACL and meniscus suffered during Week 15 last season. Prior to his injury, he compiled 12.5 sacks in 14 games (13 starts) in his first year with Green Bay.

While Green Bay Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons is reportedly poised to make his long-awaited return from his ACL injury Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Rams, he's officially listed as "questionable" for the Week 12 matchup.

In Parsons' first, abridged season with the Packers, he piled up 12.5 sacks over 14 games.

Running back Josh Jacobs is also "questionable" for the Thanksgiving Eve game at SoFi Stadium.

He's been recovering from surgery on the ring finger he fractured.

The Kansas City Chiefs have been cautious handling the groin injury that running back Kenneth Walker III is navigating.

Walker hasn't played since Nov. 8, a Week 9 win over the New York Jets.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters that Walker will return to practice Tuesday.

"We'll see how he does," Reid said, per Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star. "I'm not anticipating a ton of work there, but he'll get out there and move around."

The Chiefs will travel to Buffalo this week for a Thanksgiving showdown with the Bills.

If there's anything that can slow this 49ers team, it's the blue medical tent. Injuries have ravaged the 49ers all season, and on Sunday night, San Francisco ran out a Geriatric Avengers of thirty-somethings including George Kittle, Mike Evans, Christian McCaffrey, Deebo Samuel Sr. and Kyle Juszczyk. All that experience gives the 49ers a big-game-pressure edge that few teams can match, but it also makes them intensely vulnerable to injury. Stints on the IR are a when, not an if, for the 49ers. Right tackle Colton McKivitz was the latest as he suffered a gruesome leg injury in the first half Sunday night.

The guy ensuring all those uncs get the ball is finally receiving some attention of his own again, too. Brock Purdy hasn't shown up on MVP leaderboards since finishing fourth in his breakout season of 2023. This season ought to change that. He's among the league leaders in touchdowns, passer rating and completion percentage, among other useful stats.

Against the best defense in the NFL, all Purdy did was throw for three touchdowns and 255 yards on 21-of-26 completions. He's grown into the perfect weapon for head coach Kyle Shanahan's unorthodox offense, and Sunday was the perfect showcase.

McCarthy was asked on Monday whether he was considering a quarterback change after the offense's poor play in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

McCarthy kept it short and to the point, saying, "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback."

Pittsburgh dropped to 6-4 after the loss and fell to third place in the AFC North, trailing both the Cincinnati Bengals and the Cleveland Browns.

The Steelers had 255 yards of offense but couldn't beat the Eagles. Philadelphia's win ended a seven-game losing streak for the franchise, and the Steelers have now lost two straight games, both coming after their Week 9 bye.

In the loss, Rodgers was 30-of-44 passing for 227 yards and a touchdown. He led the team in rushing with 29 yards on five carries, but was sacked five times.

If the New England Patriots are interested in adding quarterback Daniel Jones, head coach Mike Vrabel isn't saying so.

While Jones has cleared waivers, the Patriots named Tommy DeVito as their starting QB for Week 12's matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers. However, even if New England signed Jones, he would be unlikely to take the field with them so soon after joining the team.

Taking over after Drake Maye was injured in Week 10's game versus the Detroit Lions, DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards with 1 touchdown and 1 interception. Vrabel said he was impressed by the backup QB's performance and the improvement he's shown since training camp, even if the Patriots didn't win the game.

The plan is for Sam Darnold to start against the 49ers on Sunday, but Mike Macdonald wants to see the quarterback in practice first before making a final decision.

Darnold has been out for two games due to a quad injury suffered in Week 8.

#2563. Week 12 Super Bowl stock report: 49ers separate from pack, Jaguars show imperfections

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Thanksgiving week is where the rubber meets the road in the NFL. Division races either heat up or see one team separate itself from the pack, like the San Francisco 49ers are beginning to do in the NFC West. The dust has settled on the biggest moves from this month's trade deadline, and they are either paying dividends or, in the Jacksonville Jaguars' case, raising eyebrows for their minimal impact. The sense of urgency cranks up across the league from this week forward.

The holiday itself provides two monumental collisions that will help sort the playoff race and pave the road to the Super Bowl. And just a couple of days later, the 49ers will face a critical battle as part of the traditional Sunday slate. Win that matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, and San Francisco can practically bank on reaching the postseason if not winning the division altogether.

Here are the latest trends in the Super Bowl race heading into Week 12.

General manager John Lynch reportedly agreed to terms on a contract extension with the 49ers this week. It is well deserved, because he has constructed an absolute behemoth of a team. Lynch's biggest moves of 2026 paid sizable dividends in the drubbing of the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. None were more fruitful than Mike Evans, easily among the most impactful free-agent signees of the year, who racked up 109 yards in his first game back from Achilles tendinitis.

Speaking of Achilles tendons, it's easy to forget that George Kittle tore his less than a year ago. His remarkable recovery is practically superhuman. He just turned in the best performance by a tight end against the Vikings this season with two touchdowns.

And then there is Brock Purdy. It is a close race between him and Joe Burrow for the NFL MVP award, and Sunday's showing closed any gap between the two. No quarterback had logged a passer rating above 90.0 against Minnesota all year until Purdy went nuclear on the typically ferocious defense and posted an eye-popping passer rating of 146.0. He continues to master Kyle Shanahan's offense, and his acumen has never been more obvious than it was in how he picked apart the Vikings' blitz-heavy scheme. Purdy completed 16 of 18 passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns against the blitz, and his 12.4 yards per attempt on quick passes were the most against a Brian Flores-led Vikings defense.

All of these pieces came together for the 49ers' most impressive outing of the season — one that cemented San Francisco not only at the top of the NFC but also at the front of the Super Bowl race. And the margin between them and the rest of the pack is only getting wider.

Before their 23-18 loss to the New York Giants, the Jaguars were among the buzziest teams in the league thanks to a two-loss record, a scorching offense, and a couple of trade deadline splashes. How quickly things change. The Jaguars are now two games back of the AFC's No. 1 seed instead of just one, the offense is fresh off perhaps its worst showing of the year, and Jordan Davis — who cost a first- and second-round pick at the trade deadline — was a non-factor in run defense in his team debut.

Some of those knocks against Jacksonville will prove to be one-offs in time. It is more likely than not that this squad rebounds in a big way against the Titans in Week 12 and gears up for a surge deep into the postseason. But if any of those issues persist, the most likely culprit would be the offense.

It starts up front where the offensive line is far from full strength. These three positions are of the biggest concern:

The Giants controlled the trenches, and that had a cascading effect on the rest of the Jacksonville offense. Trevor Lawrence took three sacks, faced 23 pressures, and threw two interceptions. It was his worst game by EPA this year and only his second with a negative EPA (-12.8). He was under duress all game and saw a 45% pressure rate for only the third time this season. And in the run game, the Jaguars matched their least-productive effort of the campaign with just 77 yards and saw lead running back Bhayshul Tuten sustain an ankle injury.

Little's anticipated return to action against the Titans should help the offense bounce back, at least somewhat.

There was no better time for the New York Giants to notch their best win of the season than last week, because the rest of the NFC East also won. New York maintained its divisional advantage and needs to keep stacking victories to fend off a Dallas Cowboys team that, for all its flaws, can score with anyone and a Washington Commanders squad that is rounding into form and faces a cushy schedule over the next four weeks.

The combination of John Harbaugh's rebuilt culture and the growing pool of prolific young talent on the roster creates a real playoff contender. For instance, second-year edge rusher Abdul Carter racked up a career-high 12 pressures against the Jaguars, which was the second-highest total by any player in any game all year. And behind his disruptive effort on the defensive front, the Giants logged their first win against a team five or more games above .500 since 2023, when they beat a Philadelphia Eagles team that sat most of its starters in the final week of that regular season.

The Giants will have to win their division to get into the dance. It will be another six weeks until they see another head-to-head matchup against an NFC East team, so in the meantime, they need to keep stacking efforts like the one they just displayed against a Super Bowl hopeful.

Thursday, 1 p.m., CBS, stream on Paramount+

The Detroit Lions' annual Thanksgiving game is the biggest NFC North matchup of the year to date. Every team in this division is on track to make the playoffs, but these kinds of showdowns are where Super Bowl contenders separate themselves from the average postseason hopeful. Both defenses have been better of late and need to stay that way for Detroit or Chicago to surge all the way to February, so this will be an excellent test, as they match up against some of the best offensive talent and most renowned play-callers in the NFL.

Thursday, 8:20 p.m., NBC, stream on Fubo (try for free)

A pair of franchises that have regularly butted heads during the Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes eras clash once again in the Thanksgiving finale. This battle ranks among the greatest Thanksgiving contests in league history, as the combined 17-3 record between the teams is the second-best win percentage entering a holiday game in the last 50 seasons. Allen owns a commanding 5-1 lead in regular-season games against Mahomes, while the latter is unbeaten in the postseason at 4-0. There is a strong chance that this will be the first of two meetings between the legendary quarterbacks with the second potentially sending the winner to the Super Bowl.

Sunday, 4:25 p.m., Fox, stream on Fubo (try for free)

As it stands entering Week 12, only one team from the NFC West is set to reach the postseason. That is a stunning turn of events, considering the division was initially projected to send three teams to the playoffs. Seattle is on the outside looking in, and while the gap between it and the 49ers is likely too wide to close before the end of the regular season, this would be a colossal win on the Seahawks' road back to a second consecutive championship. The 49ers took the first matchup in the Pacific Northwest and thus should feel confident about pulling off a sweep when the series heads to the Bay Area this weekend.

#2562. Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

Kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

It's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

We already know the Wild are big-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

However, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.

Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.
