#2560. Yankees And Marlins Trade Talks Could Bring Pitching Home

The New York Yankees and Miami Marlins share a clear history of making deals, and that connection points to a perfect winter trade. New York needs a reliable infielder to fill the gap left by Jazz Chisholm Jr., while Miami requires solid starting pitching to build for the future.

Per Sports Illustrated, the two teams have already completed major transactions under current leadership. The Marlins recently sent Ryan Weathers to New York in exchange for four prospects, and the deal that moved Jazz Chisholm Jr. to the Bronx included catcher Agustín Ramírez and infielders Jared Serna and Abrahan Ramírez. That working relationship means the front offices know how to negotiate.

Second baseman Otto Lopez stands out as the ideal target for the Yankees because his stats match New York's offensive struggles. Lopez posted a 115 wRC+ and a .349 on-base percentage in 2026, numbers that directly address the team's need for players who get on base. The market for hitters remains thin, which makes a player with Lopez's production even more valuable for a contender.

In return, Miami would receive right-handed pitcher Will Warren, who posted a 3.92 ERA over 156 innings in 2026. Warren also sported an 8.0% walk rate and a 44.2% ground ball percentage, showing he has the control and pitch mix to succeed in a major league rotation. The Marlins could also add prospect Ben Hess, who FanGraphs ranks as the Yankees' sixth overall prospect.

Some fans worry that trading stars always leads to a rebuild, but this deal offers a different outcome. Just Baseball noted that clichés like "A tiger can't change its stripes" or "you can't teach an old dog new tricks" often dominate the conversation about the Marlins. Those sayings suggest the team cannot change, yet the front office has shown a willingness to adapt and make moves that fit their current window.

The trade pitch from ESPN's Jorge Castillo suggests the Yankees should move outfielder Jasson Dominguez and a starting pitcher to acquire Lopez. Castillo wrote that Lopez is under team control through 2029 and is coming off a career All-Star season with 191 hits. This specific detail about his contract length gives the Marlins long‑term security if they keep him.

Trading for a player with a known track record reduces the risk for both sides. Lopez has experience at second base and can theoretically slide over to fill the position full-time. Since he finished sixth in the majors last season with a 5.9 fWAR, the Yankees need not wonder if he can withstand New York pressure.

The Marlins could use Brendan Brock, a 2027 draft pick from the University of Oklahoma, as a developable asset. During his college career, Brock recorded 55 RBIs, 13 home runs, and a .302 average across 286 at-bats. This trade allows Miami to stock their farm system while New York fills a critical hole in their lineup for the upcoming season.

#2559. Brandon Aiyuk to meet with Commanders, per report: Free agent WR seeks reunion with Jayden Daniels

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Now that wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is no longer tied to the San Francisco 49ers and is officially a free agent, he has his sights set on a new contract and a fresh start. That journey back to the field will start with the Washington Commanders. Shortly after officially clearing waivers, Aiyuk scheduled a visit with the Commanders for Wednesday, according to ESPN, a key step toward playing for the first time since 2024.

During his public spat with the 49ers in which he sought a release from his contract, Aiyuk made it abundantly clear that he preferred to sign with the Commanders. In social media posts, Aiyuk repeatedly mentioned the Commanders,  either requesting a trade to Washington or reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list with the intention of pursuing a deal with the Commanders.

Aiyuk played with star Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels in college at Arizona State, so their connection makes Washington a logical destination as he aims to rekindle a once-promising career. If any quarterback could squeeze whatever juice is left in the former first-round pick, it ought to be the one with whom he starred in college and who ranks among the NFL's top young signal-callers.

Aiyuk and Daniels got into a social media feud over the summer when Aiyuk went on a posting spree and voiced his displeasure with his situation in San Francisco, calling out Daniels and the Commanders in the process. Daniels responded by telling him to "enjoy retirement, pal," but they reportedly mended their relationship.

Prior to a devastating knee injury in 2024, Aiyuk shined over four seasons with the 49ers. He upped his receiving production year after year and peaked in 2023, racking up 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns on 75 receptions. In those campaigns before he tore his ACL and MCL, Aiyuk never posted fewer than 748 yards or five touchdowns in a season.

This is so far removed from his last game appearance; it's unclear how much Aiyuk has to offer. But if he can contribute as part of a wide receiver rotation, adding him to the roster should be enticing for the Commanders.

Washington lost its top receiver, Terry McLaurin, for the season after five games and has been thin at the wideout spot ever since. Rookie Antonio Williams is fresh off the best game of his career and is developing into a starting-caliber option, but the Commanders would still benefit from another veteran option in a room that features Stefon Diggs, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and Van Jefferson. The offense ranks in the bottom half of the league in EPA per pass at No. 21, and Monday's win over the Cincinnati Bengals marked the first time in Daniels' career that he did not record a touchdown of any kind.

#2558. Julius Randle has brutal response to Nets' blowout loss: 'One of the worst games I've ever been a part of'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Brooklyn Nets are no strangers to losing games this season, as they fell to 3-11 on Wednesday night, but in a season filled with lopsided defeats, losing by 30 points to the Chicago Bulls stood out as a new low point.

The Bulls also entered Wednesday's game at 3-10 on the season, operating as one of the league's worst teams so far, but Chicago exploded for 137 points against the Nets, with eight players reaching double figures. While Chicago's biggest issue has come on the defensive end this season, the Bulls haven't exactly been lighting opponents up offensively, sitting 23rd in the league in offensive rating.

The Nets' complete inability to put up a resistance against the Bulls rang alarm bells in Brooklyn and had veteran Julius Randle calling out his team for an "embarrassing" and "unacceptable" performance.

"I've been in the league for 13 years... that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of."Julius Randle didn't hold back after the Nets’ 30-point loss to Bulls. 😳 pic.twitter.com/s3YQ8TxP35

"The main struggle? I don't know, that was embarrassing," Randle said after the game. "Been in the league for 13 years and that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of. And not because of the score. You lose by 30 sometimes -- it's just a bad night -- but it's how we did it. That just, it wasn't cool. Nothing about it was cool. We gotta find a way to figure out the root of it or whatever, but that just is unacceptable."

Considering Randle has been on his fair share of bad basketball teams over his career in Los Angeles, New Orleans and New York, that's saying something.

There are five teams that have separated themselves from the pack at the bottom of the NBA in terms of defense and the Nets are one of them with a 119.0 defensive rating (26th in the league). No one expected much of Brooklyn on that end of the floor with the roster they've assembled, but it's one thing to have lesser talent on the defensive end; it's another to combine that with a general lack of effort.

This early in the season, the latter is a much larger concern and the Nets have now given up at least 124 points in five of their last six games. If they were able to shrug off some of those lopsided losses to quality teams as life in the NBA, Wednesday was proof that their problems extend far beyond just some schedule losses.

Giving up 137 to a Bulls team that's been similarly bad this year is, in Randle's words, unacceptable. The concern is that no one in Brooklyn, including Randle, seems quite sure what the exact problem is or how to fix it.

#2557. NFL Thanksgiving 2026: A look at every NFL halftime show performer for the holiday slate

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Thanksgiving is all about family, friends, reflecting on what you're thankful for, food, and of course, football. Pigskin and turkey have gone hand-in-hand since 1934, when the Detroit Lions' owner started the Turkey Day game tradition as a way to attract more fans.

Since then, with the exception of 1939 to 1944 (World War II), the Lions have played on the holiday. The Dallas Cowboys have played on Thanksgiving since 1966, with the exception of 1975 and 1977. This year is no different, with the Lions and Cowboys once again hosting games.

Bears vs. Lions will be played at 1 p.m. ET on CBS and stream on Paramount+. Eagles vs. Cowboys will take place at 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX, and the Chiefs and Bills face off at 8:20 p.m. on NBC.

But the entertainment isn't just what happens while the clock is running. The Thanksgiving games will also feature halftime performances. With football and music, there's something for everyone to enjoy. Plus, it's not just the Thanksgiving game getting a halftime show: the Thanksgiving Eve matchup between the Rams and Packers will also feature mid-game entertainment.

Here's a look at each halftime show performance during the holiday week:

Game: Rams vs. PackersLocation: SoFi Stadium (Inglewood, California)Time: 8 p.m. ETStreaming: Netflix

For the first time ever, NFL football will be played on Thanksgiving Eve, and U2 will take the stage at halftime. The band is celebrating their 50th anniversary and just released their 16th studio album "Carnaval De Luz," with a tour attached. The Rock & Roll Hall of Famers have 22 Grammy Awards, two Academy Award nominations, two Golden Globe Awards and many more. The group has over 300 total award show nominations with 150 wins.

This will not be the first time the group has performed during an NFL game. They took the stage for the Super Bowl XXXVI halftime performance for a moving performance that paid tribute to the victims of 9/11, which had happened just months before.

Game: Bears vs. LionsLocation: Ford Field (Detroit, Michigan)Time: 1 p.m. ETNetwork: CBSStreaming: Paramount+

The 87th Thanksgiving Day Classic will feature a performance from the legendary Wu Tang Clan. The hip-hop group has influence that goes beyond music and into fashion, film and television. They are part of the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame class of 2026 and are currently on their farewell tour. Members of the group include RZA, GZA, Method Man, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah, U-God, Masta Killa, Inspectah Deck, Cappadonna and the late Ol' Dirty Bastard (ODB).

Eminem and his longtime manager, Paul Rosenberg, selected the performer and will be executive producers of the show for the second straight year.

Game: Cowboys vs. EaglesLocation: AT&T Stadium (Arlington, Texas)Time: 4:30 p.m. ETNetwork: FOX (Stream: fubo, try for free)

Country superstar Miranda Lambert will take the stage during the break in the NFC East rival game. The halftime performance kicks off the Salvation Army's annual Red Kettle Campaign, encouraging fans to give back to those in need. This performance will mark the 30th consecutive Red Kettle Kickoff halftime show.

Lambert has 31 Grammy nominations, with three wins, 40 Academy of Country Music Awards, and 14 Country Music Association Awards. She is the most-awarded artist in the Academy of Country Music's history.

Game: Chiefs vs. BillsLocation: Highmark Stadium (Orchard Park, New York)Time: 8:20 p.m. ETNetwork: NBC (Stream: fubo, try for free)

The Bills are bringing in a hometown group to perform for the primetime Thanksgiving Day game. The band has been together for over three decades, has four Grammy nominations and holds the all-time radio record for "Most Top 10 Singles."  They have sold over 15 million records worldwide and have hits that include "Iris" and "Nothing Lasts Forever." The members of the band are John Rzeznik and Robby Takac, with past members George Tutuska and Mike Malinin.

#2556. Four New PGA Tour Cards Won With Ventus, But Not The Same Shaft

Four players secured their 2027 PGA Tour cards, and all four used a Fujikura VENTUS driver shaft. A quick glance at the equipment list might suggest a one-size-fits-all solution for aspiring pros. That view misses the point entirely. The specific model matters far more than the brand name or the flex rating printed on the label.

According to AmateurGolf.com, two of the new graduates used the VENTUS Black, one chose the TR Blue, and the fourth played the Red model. All four earned their status through the international route, yet they represent three distinct performance profiles. The 6-X flex is just the starting line, not the finish.

Golfers often fixate on the number and letter combination, assuming an X-flex is the only path to the big leagues. The reality is far more nuanced. Fujikura places the Red shaft on the higher-launching side of its lineup while the Black sits at the low end. A player can possess the swing speed for an X-flex and still need the ball to climb to find the fairway.

The data shows that the mid-amateur Kish Israni needed exactly that combination. He visited Fujikura's Carlsbad headquarters seeking more height without losing accuracy. A VENTUS Red 6-X with VeloCore+ resulted from his session, matching the model used by one of the four graduates. During his fitting, Israni observed higher flight and gained over three miles per hour in clubhead speed.

The choice of shaft color reflects a specific problem each player needed to solve. Chris Cayford arrived with a fitting goal of cutting excess driver spin. He finished with a slightly lighter TR Blue 6-X. Although his distance numbers remained unchanged, he noted it was easier to square the face. His smash factor improved as a direct result of the switch.

These two sessions prove that the tee shot dictates the club selection, not the other way around. Starting with the flex alone would mistake these golfers for candidates for the exact same build. Looking at the desired ball flight makes the choices obvious. The VENTUS Red helps a player who needs to launch it higher, while the Black helps a player who needs to keep it down.

This trend extends beyond the international graduates. Among graduates from the American circuit, Fujikura identified five additional driver shafts, representing a quarter of that group. Several VENTUS builds appear on their list, including a SPEEDER TR.

These figures provide tournament golfers with a concise list of questions to ask at the range. Is it the carry over a bunker causing you to press, or the drive starting on line and running into the rough. The answer determines the shaft, not the flex. The former FedEx Cup champ Billy Horschel still retains conditional status after a tough season. "I know I'm going to get in quite a few events and I've got to be able to take advantage of those opportunities," he said.

#2555. Sonny Gray returns to Twins on two-year, $55 million contract, per report

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Sonny Gray is heading back to Minnesota. The Twins on Wednesday announced they have signed the veteran right-hander, who spent the 2022-23 seasons with the club. It's a two-year contract worth $55 million with an opt out, reports the New York Post.

Skies are Gray but things are looking Sonny!Welcome back, Sonny Gray! pic.twitter.com/Ky2sBhVi57

Gray, 37, finished fifth in the American League Cy Young voting this season after throwing 169 innings with a 2.72 ERA and strong underlying numbers for the Boston Red Sox. He was the AL Cy Young runner-up in 2023, his final season with the Twins. All told, Gray threw 303 ⅔ innings with a 2.90 ERA during his time in Minnesota.

CBS Sports ranked Gray as the No. 14 free agent available on the market this offseason. Here's our write-up:

Gray has reportedly mulled retirement over the last few offseasons, but he intends to pitch in 2027. He's as crafty as ever, using six pitches regularly and giving hitters every look. Hard, soft, sharp break, big movement, etc. Gray's stuff works in such a way that he seems to get a quick first or second pitch out every inning, allowing him to pitch deep into games. He completed six innings 22 times in his 29 starts this past season, which makes him a workhorse by 2026 standards. Gray will pitch the entire 2027 season at age 37 and he's lost enough velocity to shrink his margin of error meaningfully, which creates some over-the-cliff risk. Still, the 14-year veteran is not out of place as the No. 2 starter in a postseason rotation.

Gray now joins a Twins rotation that includes Taj Bradley, Joe Ryan and Pablo López, who missed last season after undergoing Tommy John surgery in February. Other options include Dean Kremer, Bailey Ober and Mick Abel.

The Twins are coming off a 2026 season in which they went 77-85 with a -58 run differential. That landed them in third place in the American League Central and seven games out of the third and final wild-card spot in the AL. Although the Twins improved upon their 2025 record, they've now missed the postseason for three straight years, their longest drought in a decade. The Gray addition -- plus catcher Ryan Jeffers' acceptance of the qualifying offer for 2027 -- helps the cause, and no doubt the Twins under second-year manager Derek Shelton will be looking to get back to the playoffs in what again figures to be a winnable division.
